title.zh: 卷八十一 列傳第六 三宗諸子
title.en: Volume 81 Biographies 6: Sons of the Three Zongs (Taizong, Gaozong, and Zhongzong)
title.raw: 卷八十一 列傳第六 三宗諸子 Volume 81 Biographies 6: Sons of the Three Zongs (Taizong, Gaozong, and Zhongzong)

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 高宗八子：後宮劉生忠，鄭生孝，楊生上金，蕭淑妃生素節，武后生弘、賢、中宗皇帝、睿宗皇帝。

translations.literal: Gaozong had eight sons: Liu of the rear palace bore Zhong; Zheng bore Xiao; Yang bore Shangjin; Consort Xiao Shufei bore Sujie; Wu bore Hong, Xian, Emperor Zhongzong, and Emperor Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had eight sons: Lady Liu of the inner palace gave birth to Zhong; Lady Zheng to Xiao; Lady Yang to Shangjin; Consort Xiao Shufei to Sujie; and Empress Wu to Hong, Xian, Emperor Zhongzong, and Emperor Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 燕王忠，字正本。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan, Zhong, was styled Zhengben.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan, Zhong, bore the style name Zhengben.

sentences.zh: 帝始為太子而忠生，宴宮中，俄而太宗臨幸，詔宮臣曰：「朕始有孫，欲共為樂。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor was first crown prince, Zhong was born; they feasted in the palace, and presently Taizong came on a visit; he charged the palace officials, saying, "I now have a grandson and wish to share joy together."
translations.idiomatic: While the Emperor was still crown prince, Zhong was born. A feast was held in the palace, and soon Taizong paid a visit. He told the palace officials, "I now have a grandson and wish to share the joy with you all."

sentences.zh: 酒酣，帝起舞，以屬群臣，在位皆舞，賚賜有差。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep, the Emperor danced and handed it off to the assembled ministers; all present danced, and gifts and rewards were graded.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone deep, the Emperor danced and passed the cup to his ministers; everyone present danced, and gifts were bestowed in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十年，始王陳。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan, he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of the Zhenguan era, he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，拜雍州牧。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, he was appointed Governor of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yonghui era, he was appointed Governor of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王皇后無子，後舅柳奭說後，以忠母微，立之必親己，後然之，請於帝；

translations.literal: Empress Wang had no son; the Empress's uncle Liu Shi persuaded the Empress that because Zhong's mother was of low standing, establishing him would surely draw her close to herself; the Empress agreed and requested it of the Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang had no son. The Empress's uncle Liu Shi urged her that because Zhong's mother was of humble birth, making him heir would surely bind him to her; the Empress agreed and petitioned the Emperor;

sentences.zh: 又奭與褚遂良、韓瑗、長孫無忌、於誌寧等繼請，遂立為皇太子。

translations.literal: Liu Shi together with Chu Suiliang, Han Gui, Zhangsun Wuji, Yu Zhining, and others in succession requested it, and he was thereupon established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi, together with Chu Suiliang, Han Gui, Zhangsun Wuji, Yu Zhining, and others in succession pressed the case, and Zhong was thereupon established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 後廢，武后子弘甫三歲，許敬宗希後旨，建言：「國有正嫡，太子宜同漢劉強故事。」

translations.literal: After she was deposed, Wu's son Hong was just three years old; Xu Jingzong, to please the Empress, submitted advice: "The state has a legitimate eldest son; the crown prince should follow the Han precedent of Liu Qiang."
translations.idiomatic: After Wang was deposed, Empress Wu's son Hong was only three. Xu Jingzong, eager to please the Empress, urged that "the state has a legitimate eldest son; the crown prince ought to follow the Han precedent of Liu Qiang."

sentences.zh: 帝召見敬宗曰：「立嫡若何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Xu Jingzong and said, "How about establishing the legitimate son?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Xu Jingzong and asked, "What of establishing the legitimate heir?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「正本則萬事治，太子，國本也。

translations.literal: He replied, "When the root is correct, the myriad affairs are governed; the crown prince is the root of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "When the root is correct, all affairs are well governed; the crown prince is the root of the state.

sentences.zh: 且東宮所出微，今知有正嫡，不自安；

translations.literal: Moreover, the Eastern Palace's issue is of low standing; now knowing there is a legitimate eldest son, he will not be at ease;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the heir in the Eastern Palace is of low birth; once he knows a legitimate eldest son exists, he cannot rest easy;

sentences.zh: 竊位而不自安，非社稷計。」

translations.literal: usurping the position yet not at ease—this is not a plan for the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Holding a position he cannot keep in peace—this is no plan for the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「忠固自讓。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Zhong has indeed yielded of himself."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Zhong has indeed offered to step aside of his own accord."

sentences.zh: 敬宗曰：「能為太伯，不亦善乎？」

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong said, "To be able to act as Taibo—is that not also good?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong said, "To be able to play Taibo—is that not also a fine thing?"

sentences.zh: 於是降封梁王、梁州都督，賜甲第，實封戶二千，物二萬段。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was demoted and enfeoffed Prince of Liang and Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture, granted a fine mansion, a fief of two thousand households, and twenty thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhong was demoted and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture, granted a fine mansion, a fief of two thousand households, and twenty thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 俄徙房州刺史。

translations.literal: Presently he was transferred to Governor of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Governor of Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 忠寢懼不聊生，至衣婦人衣，備刺客。

translations.literal: Zhong lay in dread and could scarcely live; he even wore women's clothes and kept assassins at the ready.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong lived in dread and could scarcely endure; he even wore women's clothing and kept assassins at hand.

sentences.zh: 數有妖夢，嘗自占。

translations.literal: Several times he had demonic dreams and once divined for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He had demonic dreams again and again and once performed divination for himself.

sentences.zh: 事露，廢為庶人，囚黔州承乾故宅。

translations.literal: When the matter was exposed, he was deposed to commoner status and imprisoned in the former residence of Chengqian at Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, he was deposed to commoner status and imprisoned in Chengqian's former residence at Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，宦者王伏勝得罪於武后，敬宗乃誣忠及上官儀與伏勝謀反，賜死，年二十二。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Linde, the eunuch Wang Fusheng offended Empress Wu; Xu Jingzong then falsely charged Zhong and Shangguan Yi with Fusheng in plotting rebellion; he was ordered to die, aged twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Linde era, the eunuch Wang Fusheng offended Empress Wu. Xu Jingzong then falsely charged Zhong and Shangguan Yi with Fusheng of plotting rebellion; Zhong was ordered to die, aged twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 明年，太子弘表請收葬，許之。

translations.literal: The next year, Crown Prince Hong memorialized requesting burial; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Crown Prince Hong memorialized requesting that he be buried; permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追封，又贈太尉、揚州大都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, posthumous enfeoffment was granted, and he was also given the posthumous title Grand Preceptor and Grand Military Commissioner of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shenlong era he received posthumous enfeoffment, and was also granted the posthumous titles Grand Preceptor and Grand Military Commissioner of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 原王原悼王孝，永徽元年，始王許，與杞、雍二王同封。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuan Prince of Yuan, posthumous name Xiaowang Xiao, in the first year of Yonghui was first enfeoffed Prince of Xu, enfeoffed together with the Princes of Qi and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuan, the posthumous Prince Xiaowang Xiao: in the first year of Yonghui he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, together with the Princes of Qi and Yong.

sentences.zh: 早薨。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追封及謚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous title were granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong he received posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 澤王澤王上金，始王杞。

translations.literal: Prince of Ze Prince of Ze Shangjin was first enfeoffed Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ze Shangjin was first enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，遙領益州大都督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui he held the title Grand Military Commissioner of Yi Prefecture at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yonghui he held the distant appointment as Grand Military Commissioner of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷鄜、壽二州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Governor of Fu and Shou prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Governor of Fu and Shou prefectures.

sentences.zh: 武后疾其母，故有司誣奏，削封邑，徙置澧州。

translations.literal: Empress Wu hated his mother; therefore the authorities falsely memorialized, reduced his fief, and transferred him to Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu hated his mother; the authorities therefore falsely memorialized against him, reduced his fief, and transferred him to Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，後陽若可喜者，表杞王上金、鄱陽王素節聽朝集，義陽、宣城二公主各增夫秩。

translations.literal: After a long while the Empress feigned pleasure; she memorialized that Prince of Qi Shangjin and Prince of Poyang Sujie might attend court assemblies, and that the Princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng each should have their husbands' ranks raised.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval the Empress feigned pleasure and memorialized that Prince of Qi Shangjin and Prince of Poyang Sujie might attend court assemblies, and that the Princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng should each have their husbands' ranks raised.

sentences.zh: 由是上金為沔州刺史，素節岳州刺史，然卒不朝。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shangjin became Governor of Mian Prefecture and Sujie Governor of Yue Prefecture, yet in the end they did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Shangjin became Governor of Mian Prefecture and Sujie Governor of Yue Prefecture, yet in the end they never came to court.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，詔上金、素節、二公主赴哀。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died, an edict summoned Shangjin, Sujie, and the two princesses to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, an edict summoned Shangjin, Sujie, and the two princesses to come mourn.

sentences.zh: 文明元年，徙王畢，又徙王澤。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wenming he was transferred to Prince of Bi, then again to Prince of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wenming he was transferred to Prince of Bi, then again to Prince of Ze.

sentences.zh: 歷五州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as governor of five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 載初中，武承嗣諷周興誣上金、素節謀反，召系御史獄。

translations.literal: In the early Zaichu era, Wu Chengsi prompted Zhou Xing to falsely charge Shangjin and Sujie with rebellion; they were summoned and detained in the censor's prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zaichu era Wu Chengsi prompted Zhou Xing to falsely charge Shangjin and Sujie with rebellion; they were summoned and held in the censor's prison.

sentences.zh: 上金聞素節已被殺，即雉經，七子並流死顯州。

translations.literal: Shangjin heard that Sujie had already been killed and immediately hanged himself; his seven sons were all exiled to death at Xian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Shangjin heard that Sujie had already been killed, he at once hanged himself; his seven sons were all exiled and died at Xian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追還官爵，以子義珣嗣王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong his offices and titles were posthumously restored, and his son Yixun succeeded to the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong his offices and titles were posthumously restored, and his son Yixun succeeded to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 義珣始被謫，匿身為傭保，而嗣許王瓘〗利其爵邑，告義珣假冒，復流嶺外。

translations.literal: Yixun, at first exiled, hid himself as a hired laborer; the successor Prince of Xu Guan coveted his title and fief and reported that Yixun was an impostor; he was again exiled beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Yixun, at first exiled, hid himself working as a hired laborer; the successor Prince of Xu Guan coveted his title and fief and reported Yixun as an impostor, and he was again exiled beyond the ranges.

sentences.zh: 開元初，以素節子璆為後，而玉真公主表義珣實上金子，乃奪璆爵，復使義珣嗣王，拜率更令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Sujie's son Qiu was made heir; but Princess Yuzhen memorialized that Yixun was truly Shangjin's son; Qiu's title was then taken away and Yixun was again made to succeed, appointed Director of the Court of the Crown Prince's Sons.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaiyuan, Sujie's son Qiu was made heir; but Princess Yuzhen memorialized that Yixun was truly Shangjin's son; Qiu's title was then stripped and Yixun was again made to succeed, appointed Director of the Court of the Crown Prince's Sons.

sentences.zh: 薨，子潓嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Juan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Juan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 許王素節，始王雍，授雍州牧。

translations.literal: Prince of Xu Prince of Xu Sujie was first enfeoffed Prince of Yong and appointed Governor of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xu Sujie was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yong and appointed Governor of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 方羈丱，即誦書日千言。

translations.literal: While still in swaddling clothes he could recite books at a thousand characters a day.
translations.idiomatic: While still in swaddling clothes he could recite a thousand characters of text per day.

sentences.zh: 師事徐齊聃，淬勉自強，帝愛之。

translations.literal: He took Xu Qiluan as teacher, tempering himself with strenuous effort; the Emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Xu Qiluan, tempering himself with strenuous effort; the Emperor cherished him.

sentences.zh: 轉岐州刺史，更王郇。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Qi Prefecture and re-enfeoffed Prince of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Qi Prefecture and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xun.

sentences.zh: 母被譖死，出素節為申州刺史。

translations.literal: When his mother was slandered to death, Sujie was sent out as Governor of Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was slandered to her death, Sujie was sent out as Governor of Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，詔素節病無入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng, an edict said Sujie was ill and need not enter court.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qianfeng an edict declared that Sujie was ill and need not enter court.

sentences.zh: 而實不病，乃著《忠孝論》自明。

translations.literal: But in fact he was not ill; he thereupon composed the "Treatise on Loyalty and Filial Piety" to make himself clear.
translations.idiomatic: But in fact he was not ill; he thereupon composed the Treatise on Loyalty and Filial Piety to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍張柬之以聞，欲帝省其誣，武后滋不悅，坐受賕降王鄱陽，削封戶什七，徙置袁州，錮終身。

translations.literal: Army Aide Zhang Jianzhi reported it, wishing the Emperor would examine the false charge; Empress Wu was all the more displeased; he was demoted for accepting bribes to Prince of Poyang, his fief households were cut by seven-tenths, he was transferred to Yuan Prefecture, and confined for life.
translations.idiomatic: Army Aide Zhang Jianzhi reported it, hoping the Emperor would see through the false charge; Empress Wu was all the more displeased; he was demoted for accepting bribes to Prince of Poyang, his fief was cut by seven-tenths, he was transferred to Yuan Prefecture, and confined for life.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年，為岳州刺史，更王葛，又徙王，歷三州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yifeng he was Governor of Yue Prefecture, re-enfeoffed Prince of Ge, again transferred princedom, and served as governor of three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yifeng he was Governor of Yue Prefecture, re-enfeoffed as Prince of Ge, again transferred in princedom, and served as governor of three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 與上金同追逮赴都，道聞遭喪哭者，謂左右曰：「病死何可得，而須哭哉？」

translations.literal: Together with Shangjin he was summoned and pursued to the capital; on the road he heard mourners crying and said to his attendants, "Death by illness—how could one obtain that? Yet one must weep?"
translations.idiomatic: Together with Shangjin he was summoned and escorted toward the capital; on the road he heard mourners wailing and said to his attendants, "Death by illness—who could hope for that? Yet must one weep?"

sentences.zh: 至龍門驛被縊，年四十三，葬以庶人禮。

translations.literal: At Longmen Post he was strangled, aged forty-three; he was buried with the rites of a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: At Longmen Post he was strangled, aged forty-three; he was buried with commoner's rites.

sentences.zh: 子瑛等九人並誅，惟琳、瓘、璆、欽古尚幼，長囚雷州。

translations.literal: His sons Ying and eight others were all executed; only Lin, Guan, Qiu, and Qingu were still young and were long imprisoned at Lei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Ying and eight others were all executed; only Lin, Guan, Qiu, and Qingu were still young and were long imprisoned at Lei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中宗復位，追故封，又贈開府儀同三司、許州刺史，陪葬乾陵。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was restored, former titles were posthumously restored, and he was also given the posthumous office of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes and Governor of Xu Prefecture, buried with honor at Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was restored, former titles were posthumously restored, and he was also granted the posthumous office of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes and Governor of Xu Prefecture, buried with honor at Qianling.

sentences.zh: 詔瓘嗣王，實封戶四百。

translations.literal: An edict had Guan succeed to the princedom with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Guan succeed to the princedom with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 開元初，封琳為嗣越王，璆嗣澤王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Lin was enfeoffed successor Prince of Yue and Qiu successor Prince of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaiyuan, Lin was enfeoffed as successor Prince of Yue and Qiu as successor Prince of Ze.

sentences.zh: 琳至右監門衛將軍，子隨封夔國公。

translations.literal: Lin reached Right General of the Right Majestic Gate Guard; his son Sui was enfeoffed Duke of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Lin rose to Right General of the Right Majestic Gate Guard; his son Sui was enfeoffed Duke of Kui.

sentences.zh: 瓘為衛尉卿，以抑上金子不得封，貶鄂州別駕。

translations.literal: Guan was Minister of the Court for the Imperial Clan but, because he had suppressed Shangjin's son from receiving enfeoffment, was demoted Vice Prefect of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was Minister of the Court for the Imperial Clan but, because he had blocked Shangjin's son from receiving enfeoffment, was demoted Vice Prefect of E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 因詔外繼嗣王者皆歸宗，乃以嗣江王祎為信安王，嗣蜀王𥙆為廣漢王，嗣密王徹為濮陽王，嗣曹王臻為濟國公，嗣趙王琚為中山王，武陽王繼宗為澧國公。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict said all who succeeded to princedom from outside the line should return to their clans; thereupon successor Prince of Jiang Yi was made Prince of Xin'an, successor Prince of Shu 𥙆 Prince of Guanghan, successor Prince of Mi Che Prince of Puyang, successor Prince of Cao Zhen Duke of Ji, successor Prince of Zhao Ju Prince of Zhongshan, and Prince of Wuyang Jizong Duke of Li.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict declared that all who had succeeded to princedom from outside the direct line should return to their clans; successor Prince of Jiang Yi was made Prince of Xin'an, successor Prince of Shu 𥙆 Prince of Guanghan, successor Prince of Mi Che Prince of Puyang, successor Prince of Cao Zhen Duke of Ji, successor Prince of Zhao Ju Prince of Zhongshan, and Prince of Wuyang Jizong Duke of Li.

sentences.zh: 瓘累遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: Guan was repeatedly promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was repeatedly promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈蜀郡大都督。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously given Grand Military Commissioner of Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made Grand Military Commissioner of Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 二子解、需皆幼，以璆子益嗣。

translations.literal: His two sons Jie and Xu were both young; Qiu's son Yi was made to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Jie and Xu were both young; Qiu's son Yi was made to succeed.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四載，解始襲封王。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao, Jie first inherited the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao, Jie first inherited the princedom.

sentences.zh: 璆，初封嗣澤王，降為郢國公，宮宗正、光祿卿，進封褒信王。

translations.literal: Qiu, at first enfeoffed successor Prince of Ze, was reduced to Duke of Ying, served as Director of the Imperial Clan and Minister of Splendid Affairs, and advanced to Prince of Baoxin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was at first enfeoffed successor Prince of Ze, reduced to Duke of Ying, served as Director of the Imperial Clan and Minister of Splendid Affairs, and advanced to Prince of Baoxin.

sentences.zh: 初，張九齡撰《龍池頌》，刊石興慶宮，宗子以為不稱盛德，更命璆為頌，建花萼樓北。

translations.literal: At first Zhang Jiuling composed the "Ode to the Dragon Pool," carved on stone at Xingqing Palace; the imperial clansmen thought it did not match the sovereign's virtue, and Qiu was ordered to compose a new ode, erected north of the Hua'e Tower.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhang Jiuling composed the Ode to the Dragon Pool, carved in stone at Xingqing Palace; the imperial clansmen thought it ill matched the sovereign's virtue, and Qiu was ordered to compose a new ode, erected north of the Hua'e Tower.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，復拜宗正卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was again appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he was again appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 性友弟聰敏，宗子有一善，無不薦延，故宗室在省闥者多璆所啟。

translations.literal: By nature friendly, brotherly, and clever, whenever a clansman had any merit he never failed to recommend and advance him; therefore many of the imperial clan within the inner offices were ones Qiu had brought forward.
translations.idiomatic: By nature friendly, brotherly, and clever, whenever a clansman had any merit he never failed to recommend and advance him; therefore many of the imperial clan serving within the inner offices were men Qiu had brought forward.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈江陵郡大都督。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously given Grand Military Commissioner of Jiangling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made Grand Military Commissioner of Jiangling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 三子：謙為郢國公、梓州刺史，巽汝南郡公。

translations.literal: Three sons: Qian was Duke of Ying and Governor of Zi Prefecture; Xun Duke of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Three sons: Qian was Duke of Ying and Governor of Zi Prefecture; Xun Duke of Runan.

sentences.zh: 欽古封巳國公，子賁嗣。

translations.literal: Qingu was enfeoffed Duke of Si; his son Ben succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qingu was enfeoffed Duke of Si; his son Ben succeeded.

sentences.zh: 孝敬皇帝孝敬皇帝弘，永徽六年始王代，與潞王同封。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaojing Emperor Xiaojing Hong, in the sixth year of Yonghui was first enfeoffed Prince of Dai, enfeoffed together with the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Filial and Respectful Emperor Hong: in the sixth year of Yonghui he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Dai, together with the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing he was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 受《春秋左氏》於率更令郭瑜，至楚世子商臣弒其君，喟而廢卷曰：「聖人垂訓，何書此邪？」

translations.literal: He received the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn from Director of the Court of the Crown Prince's Sons Guo Yu; when he came to the Chu heir Shangchen murdering his lord, he sighed and cast aside the scroll, saying, "The sage left instruction—why does this book record such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn under Director Guo Yu; when he came to the Chu heir Shangchen murdering his lord, he sighed and cast the scroll aside, saying, "The sage left instruction—why does this book record such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 瑜曰：「孔子作《春秋》，善惡必書，褒善以勸，貶惡以誡，故商臣之罪雖千載猶不得滅。」

translations.literal: Yu said, "Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn; good and evil must be written; praising the good to encourage and condemning the evil to warn—therefore Shangchen's crime, though a thousand years pass, still cannot be extinguished."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn; good and evil must be written; praising the good to encourage and condemning the evil to warn—therefore Shangchen's crime, though a thousand years pass, still cannot be wiped away."

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「然所不忍聞，願讀它書。」

translations.literal: Hong said, "Yet what I cannot bear to hear—I wish to read another book."
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "Yet what I cannot bear to hear—I wish to read another book."

sentences.zh: 瑜拜曰：「裏名勝母，曾子不入。

translations.literal: Yu bowed and said, "A lane named Shengmu—Zengzi would not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Yu bowed and said, "A lane named Shengmu—Zengzi would not enter it.

sentences.zh: 殿下睿孝天資，黜凶悖之跡，不存視聽。

translations.literal: Your Highness is by nature wise and filial; banish the traces of fierce perversity and do not keep them in sight or hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is by nature wise and filial; banish the traces of fierce perversity and do not keep them in sight or hearing.

sentences.zh: 臣聞安上治民，莫善於禮，故孔子稱『不學禮，無以立』。

translations.literal: I have heard that to settle the superiors and govern the people, nothing is better than ritual; therefore Confucius said, "Without learning ritual, one cannot stand."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to settle the superiors and govern the people, nothing is better than ritual; therefore Confucius said, "Without learning ritual, one cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 請改受《禮》。」

translations.literal: Please change to receiving the Rites."
translations.idiomatic: Please change to studying the Rites instead."

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The crown prince said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 四年，加元服。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he received the capping ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he received the capping ceremony.

sentences.zh: 又命賓客許敬宗、右庶子許圉師、中書侍郎上官儀、中舍人楊思儉即文思殿摘采古今文章，號《瑤山玉彩》，凡五百篇。

translations.literal: He was also ordered that his guests Xu Jingzong, Right Vice President of the Heir Apparent Xu Yuanshi, Vice Minister of the Secretariat Shangguan Yi, and Attendant Gentleman Yang Sijian should at the Hall of Literary Thought gather and select articles ancient and modern, titled Jade Splendor of Mount Yao, five hundred pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered that his tutors Xu Jingzong, Right Vice President of the Heir Apparent Xu Yuanshi, Vice Minister of the Secretariat Shangguan Yi, and Attendant Gentleman Yang Sijian should at the Hall of Literary Thought gather and select articles ancient and modern, titled Jade Splendor of Mount Yao, five hundred pieces in all.

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝賜物三萬段，余臣賜有差。

translations.literal: When the book was presented, the Emperor bestowed thirty thousand bolts of goods; the remaining ministers received graded gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was presented, the Emperor bestowed thirty thousand bolts of goods; the remaining ministers received graded gifts.

sentences.zh: 又詔五日一赴光順門決事。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to attend the Guangshun Gate every five days to decide affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to attend the Guangshun Gate every five days to decide affairs.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，釋采國學，請贈顏回為太子少師，曾參太子少保，制可。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zongzhang he performed the capping rite at the Imperial Academy and requested posthumous titles for Yan Hui as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Zeng Shen as Junior Protector of the Heir Apparent; the decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zongzhang he performed the capping rite at the Imperial Academy and requested posthumous titles for Yan Hui as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Zeng Shen as Junior Protector of the Heir Apparent; the decree approved.

sentences.zh: 會有司以征遼士亡命及亡命不即首者，身殊死，家屬沒官。

translations.literal: It happened that the authorities, regarding soldiers who had fled from the Liaodong campaign and deserters who did not promptly surrender, imposed death by dismemberment and confiscation of families into government service.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the authorities, regarding soldiers who had fled from the Liaodong campaign and deserters who did not promptly surrender, imposed death by dismemberment and confiscation of families into government service.

sentences.zh: 弘諫以為「士遇病不及期，或被略若溺、壓死，而軍法不因戰亡，則同隊悉坐，法家曰亡命，而家屬與真亡者同沒。

translations.literal: Hong remonstrated, holding that "when soldiers met illness and could not reach the deadline, or were seized as in drowning or crushing death, yet military law did not treat battle death, then the whole squad was punished; the legalists called it desertion, yet families were confiscated like true deserters.
translations.idiomatic: Hong remonstrated that "when soldiers fell ill and could not reach the deadline, or were seized as in drowning or crushing, yet military law did not treat battle deaths, the whole squad was punished; the legalists called it desertion, yet families were confiscated like true deserters.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『與殺不辜，寧失不經。』

translations.literal: The Classic says, "Better to lose the inconstant than to kill the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says, 'Better to lose the inconstant than to kill the innocent.'

sentences.zh: 臣請條別其科，無使淪胥」。

translations.literal: Your servant requests separate statutes for each case, lest all be dragged down together."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant requests separate statutes for each case, lest all be dragged down together."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 帝幸東都，詔監國。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited the eastern capital, an edict appointed Hong to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor visited the eastern capital, an edict appointed Hong to oversee the state.

sentences.zh: 時關中饑，弘視廡下兵食有榆皮、蓬實者，悄然命家令寺給米。

translations.literal: At the time Guanzhong suffered famine; Hong saw soldiers under the granary eating elm bark and fleabane seeds and quietly ordered the Director of the Palace Domestic Service to supply rice.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Guanzhong suffered famine; Hong saw soldiers under the granary eating elm bark and fleabane seeds and quietly ordered the Director of the Palace Domestic Service to supply rice.

sentences.zh: 義陽、宣城二公主以母故幽掖廷，四十不嫁，弘聞眙惻，建請下降。

translations.literal: The Princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng, because of their mother, were confined in the Rear Palace; at forty they were still unmarried; Hong heard and was deeply moved, and memorialized requesting they be given in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Princesses of Yiyang and Xuancheng, because of their mother, were confined in the Rear Palace; at forty they were still unmarried; Hong heard and was deeply moved, and memorialized requesting they be given in marriage.

sentences.zh: 武后怒，即以當上衛士配之，由是失愛。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was angry and immediately matched them to palace guards on duty; thereby he lost favor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was angry and immediately matched them to palace guards on duty; thereby he lost favor.

sentences.zh: 又請以同州沙苑分假貧民。

translations.literal: He also requested that the Shayan pasture of Tong Prefecture be divided and lent to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that the Shayan pasture of Tong Prefecture be divided and lent to the poor.

sentences.zh: 會納妃裴，而有司奏贄用白雁，適苑中獲之，帝喜曰：「漢獲硃雁，為樂府歌。

translations.literal: When he was taking a consort, Pei, the authorities memorialized that the betrothal gift should use a white goose; it happened that one was obtained in the park; the Emperor rejoiced and said, "Han obtained a vermilion goose and made a Music Bureau song.
translations.idiomatic: When he was taking a consort, Pei, the authorities memorialized that the betrothal gift should use a white goose; it happened that one was obtained in the park; the Emperor rejoiced and said, "Han obtained a vermilion goose and made a Music Bureau song.

sentences.zh: 今得白雁為婚贄，婚乃人倫首，我則無慚。」

translations.literal: Now obtaining a white goose as a marriage gift—marriage is the head of human relations; I am without shame."
translations.idiomatic: Now obtaining a white goose as a marriage gift—marriage is the head of human relations; I have no cause for shame."

sentences.zh: 禮畢，曲赦岐州。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, a partial amnesty was granted for Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, a partial amnesty was granted for Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗語侍臣：「弘仁孝，賓禮大臣，未嘗有過。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once told his attendants, "Hong is benevolent and filial, treats great ministers with guest ritual, and has never had a fault."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once told his attendants, "Hong is benevolent and filial, treats great ministers with guest ritual, and has never had a fault."

sentences.zh: 而後將騁誌，弘奏請數怫旨。

translations.literal: Yet afterward, when the Empress was about to pursue her ambitions, Hong's memorials and requests repeatedly went against her will.
translations.idiomatic: Yet afterward, when Empress Wu was about to pursue her ambitions, Hong's memorials and petitions repeatedly ran counter to her wishes.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，從幸合璧宮，遇耽薨，年二十四，天下莫不痛之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, following the Emperor to Hebi Palace, he encountered Dan's death; aged twenty-four; all under heaven grieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shangyuan, while accompanying the Emperor to Hebi Palace, he fell ill and died, aged twenty-four; the whole realm mourned him.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太子嬰沈瘵，朕須其痊復，將遜於位。

translations.literal: An edict said, "The crown prince from infancy has been sunk in chronic illness; I need his recovery and intend to yield the throne.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "The crown prince has been gravely ill since infancy; I need him to recover and intend to yield the throne to him.

sentences.zh: 弘性仁厚，既承命，因感結，疾日以加。

translations.literal: Hong was by nature benevolent and generous; having received the command, he was moved to deep feeling and his illness daily grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was by nature benevolent and generous; having received the command, he was deeply moved, and his illness grew worse day by day.

sentences.zh: 宜申往命，謚為孝敬皇帝。」

translations.literal: The former command should be proclaimed; his posthumous title is Emperor Xiaojing."
translations.idiomatic: The former command should be proclaimed; he was given the posthumous title Filial and Respectful Emperor."

sentences.zh: 葬緱氏，墓號恭陵，制度盡用天子禮，百官從權制三十六日釋服。

translations.literal: He was buried at Gongshi; the tomb was named Gong Mausoleum; the regulations wholly used the rites of a Son of Heaven; the hundred officials followed the provisional rule of laying aside mourning after thirty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Gongshi; the tomb was named Gong Mausoleum; the regulations wholly followed the rites of a Son of Heaven; officials followed the provisional rule of laying aside mourning after thirty-six days.

sentences.zh: 帝自制《睿德紀》，刻石陵側。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself composed the "Record of Sagely Virtue" and had it carved in stone beside the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor himself composed the Record of Sagely Virtue and had it carved in stone beside the mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 營陵費巨億，人厭苦之，投石傷所部官司，至相率亡去。

translations.literal: Building the mausoleum cost hundreds of millions; people were weary and distressed; they cast stones and injured the officials in charge, until they fled in bands.
translations.idiomatic: Building the mausoleum cost hundreds of millions; the people were worn down and distressed; they hurled stones and injured the officials in charge, until they fled in bands.

sentences.zh: 妃薨，謚哀皇后。

translations.literal: The consort died; her posthumous title was Empress Ai.
translations.idiomatic: When the consort died, she was given the posthumous title Empress Ai.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，以楚王隆基嗣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchang, Prince of Chu Longji was made his successor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongchang era, Prince of Chu Longji was made his successor.

sentences.zh: 中宗立，詔以主祔太廟，號義宗。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, an edict had the principal spirit enshrined in the ancestral temple, titled Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, an edict enshrined Hong in the ancestral temple under the title Yizong.

sentences.zh: 開元中，有司奏：「孝敬皇帝宜建廟東都，以謚名廟。」

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, the relevant offices memorialized: "The Xiaojing Emperor should have a temple built in the Eastern Capital, naming the temple after his posthumous title."
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era, the relevant offices memorialized: "The Filial and Respectful Emperor should have a temple built in the Eastern Capital, with the temple named after his posthumous title."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 於是罷義宗號。

translations.literal: Thereupon the title Yizong was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the title Yizong was abolished.

sentences.zh: 妃即裴居道女，有婦德，而居道以妃故拜內史納言，歷太子少保、翼國公，為酷吏所陷，下獄死。

translations.literal: The consort was the daughter of Pei Judao; she had wifely virtue; Judao because of the consort was appointed Neishi Nayyan, served as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Duke of Yi, was framed by cruel officials, imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was Pei Judao's daughter, renowned for wifely virtue; because of her, Judao was appointed Inner Palace Grand Counselor, later served as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Duke of Yi, but was framed by cruel officials, thrown into prison, and died there.

sentences.zh: 章懷太子賢字明允。

translations.literal: Zhanghuai Crown Prince — Crown Prince Xian, style name Mingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhanghuai — Prince Xian, whose style name was Mingyun.

sentences.zh: 容止端重，少為帝愛。

translations.literal: His bearing and deportment were dignified and grave; from youth the Emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Dignified and grave in bearing and deportment, he was beloved by the Emperor from childhood.

sentences.zh: 甫數歲，讀書一覽輒不忘，至《論語》「賢賢易色」，一再誦之。

translations.literal: Hardly a few years old, in reading a single glance and he forgot nothing; reaching the Analects passage "to value virtue over beauty," he recited it again and again.
translations.idiomatic: While still only a few years old, he could read a text once and never forget it; when he came to the Analects passage "on valuing virtue over beauty," he recited it over and over.

sentences.zh: 帝問故，對曰：「性實愛此。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; he replied: "By nature I truly love this."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked why; he replied, "It is my nature to love this passage."

sentences.zh: 帝語李世勣，稱其夙敏。

translations.literal: The Emperor told Li Shiji, praising his precocious intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Li Shiji and praised the boy's precocious intelligence.

sentences.zh: 始王潞，歷幽州都督、雍州牧。

translations.literal: First enfeoffed as Prince of Lu; successively served as Protector-General of Youzhou and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Lu and later served as Protector-General of Youzhou and Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙王沛，累進揚州大都督、右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Transferred to Prince of Pei; cumulatively promoted to Grand Protector-General of Yangzhou and General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prince of Pei and eventually promoted to Grand Protector-General of Yangzhou and General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 更名德。

translations.literal: His name was changed to De.
translations.idiomatic: His name was changed to De.

sentences.zh: 徙王雍，仍領雍州牧、涼州大都督，實封千戶。

translations.literal: Transferred to Prince of Yong; still held the posts of Governor of Yongzhou and Grand Protector-General of Liangzhou; actual fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prince of Yong while retaining the posts of Governor of Yongzhou and Grand Protector-General of Liangzhou, with an actual fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 上元年，復名賢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, his name was restored to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan, his name was restored to Xian.

sentences.zh: 是時，皇太子薨，其六月，立賢為皇太子。

translations.literal: At this time the crown prince died; in the sixth month, Xian was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the crown prince died; in the sixth month Xian was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 俄詔監國，賢於處決尤明審，朝廷稱焉，帝手敕褒賜。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to oversee the state; Xian in adjudicating cases was especially clear and thorough; the court praised him; the Emperor personally wrote an edict commending and rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to oversee state affairs; in adjudicating cases Xian was especially clear and thorough, winning praise at court, and the Emperor personally wrote an edict commending and rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 賢又招集諸儒：左庶子張大安、洗馬劉訥言、洛州司戶參軍格希玄、學士許叔牙成玄一史藏諸周寶寧等，共註范曄《後漢書》。

translations.literal: Xian also gathered various Confucians: Left Guardian Zhang Da'an, Groom Liu Neyan, Clerk of Luozhou Revenue Ge Xixuan, Academicians Xu Shuya, Cheng Xuanyi, Shi Cangzhu, Zhou Baoning, and others, jointly annotating Fan Ye's Book of Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Xian also gathered a circle of scholars — Left Guardian Zhang Da'an, Groom Liu Neyan, Luozhou Revenue Clerk Ge Xixuan, and Academicians Xu Shuya, Cheng Xuanyi, Shi Cangzhu, and Zhou Baoning — to annotate Fan Ye's Book of Later Han together.

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝優賜段物數萬。

translations.literal: When the book was submitted, the Emperor generously bestowed tens of thousands of bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the annotated work was submitted, the Emperor generously bestowed tens of thousands of bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 時正諫大夫明崇儼以左道為武后所信，崇儼言英王類太宗，而相王貴，賢聞，惡之。

translations.literal: At the time Remonstrating Grandee Ming Chongyan, by heterodox arts, was trusted by Empress Wu; Chongyan said the Prince of Ying resembled Taizong, while the Prince of Xiang was noble; Xian heard and hated it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Remonstrating Grandee Ming Chongyan, who practiced heterodox arts, enjoyed Empress Wu's trust; when Chongyan said the Prince of Ying resembled Emperor Taizong while the Prince of Xiang was the more exalted, Xian heard of it and took offense.

sentences.zh: 宮人或傳賢乃後姊韓國夫人所生，賢益疑，而後撰《少陽政範》、《孝子傳》賜賢，數以書讓勒，愈不安。

translations.literal: Palace women also circulated that Xian was born of the Empress's elder sister, Lady of Han; Xian grew more suspicious; the Empress compiled the Shaoyang Political Canon and Biographies of Filial Sons and bestowed them on Xian, repeatedly admonishing him by letter, and he grew ever more uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women also circulated the rumor that Xian was born to the Empress's elder sister, the Lady of Han; Xian grew more suspicious still, and when the Empress composed the Shaoyang Political Canon and Biographies of Filial Sons and bestowed them on him, repeatedly admonishing him in writing, he grew ever more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 調露中，天子在東都，崇儼為盜所殺，後疑出賢謀，遣人發太子陰事，詔薛元超、裴炎、高智周雜治之，獲甲數百首於東宮。

translations.literal: In the Diaolu era, the Son of Heaven was in the Eastern Capital; Chongyan was killed by bandits; the Empress suspected the plot came from Xian; she sent men to expose the crown prince's secret affairs; she ordered Xue Yuanchao, Pei Yan, and Gao Zhizhou jointly to investigate; several hundred sets of armor were seized in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Diaolu era, while the Son of Heaven was in the Eastern Capital, Chongyan was killed by bandits; the Empress suspected Xian's involvement and sent men to expose the crown prince's secret affairs, ordering Xue Yuanchao, Pei Yan, and Gao Zhizhou to investigate jointly; several hundred sets of armor were found in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝素愛賢，薄其罪，後曰：「賢懷逆，大義滅親，不可赦。」

translations.literal: The Emperor had always loved Xian and lightened his guilt; the Empress said: "Xian harbors rebellion; great righteousness destroys kin; he cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had always loved Xian and wished to lighten his guilt, but the Empress said, "Xian harbors treason; where great righteousness is at stake, even kin must be destroyed — he cannot be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 乃廢為庶人，焚甲天津橋，貶大安普州刺史，流訥言於振州，坐徙者十餘人。

translations.literal: He was then deposed to commoner status; the armor was burned at Tianjin Bridge; Da'an was demoted to Prefect of Puzhou; Neyan was exiled to Zhenzhou; more than ten were implicated and banished.
translations.idiomatic: He was then deposed to commoner status; the armor was burned at Tianjin Bridge; Da'an was demoted to Prefect of Puzhou, Neyan was exiled to Zhenzhou, and more than ten others were implicated and banished.

sentences.zh: 開耀元年，徙賢巴州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyao, Xian was transferred to Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiyao, Xian was transferred to Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 武后得政，詔左金吾將軍丘神勣檢衛賢第，迫令自殺，年三十四。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu seized power, she ordered Left Jinwu General Qiu Shenji to guard Xian's residence and forced him to kill himself; aged thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wu seized power, she ordered Left Jinwu General Qiu Shenji to guard Xian's residence and forced him to commit suicide; he was thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 後舉哀顯福門，貶神勣疊州刺史，追復舊王。

translations.literal: Later she held mourning at Xianfu Gate; Shenji was demoted to Prefect of Diezhou; Xian's original princely rank was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later she held mourning rites at Xianfu Gate, demoted Shenji to Prefect of Diezhou, and posthumously restored Xian's original princely rank.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，贈司徒，遣使迎喪，陪葬乾陵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor; envoys were sent to bring back the coffin; buried alongside at Qian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor; envoys were sent to retrieve his remains, and he was buried alongside Emperor Gaozong at Qian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，追贈皇太子及謚。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he was posthumously made crown prince and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Xian was posthumously elevated to crown prince and given a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 三子：光順、守禮、守義。

translations.literal: Three sons: Guangshun, Shouli, and Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Guangshun, Shouli, and Shouyi.

sentences.zh: 光順為樂安王，徙義豐，被誅。

translations.literal: Guangshun was Prince of Le'an; transferred to Yifeng; was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshun was Prince of Le'an, transferred to Yifeng, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 守義為犍為王，徙封桂陽，薨。

translations.literal: Shouyi was Prince of Qianwei; transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Guiyang; died.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was Prince of Qianwei, later transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Guiyang, and died.

sentences.zh: 先天中，追封光順莒王，守義畢王。

translations.literal: In the Xiantian era, Guangshun was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ju; Shouyi as Prince of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantian era, Guangshun was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ju and Shouyi as Prince of Bi.

sentences.zh: 守禮嗣王，始名光仁，授太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Shouli succeeded to the princely line; originally named Guangren; appointed Crown Prince's Groom.
translations.idiomatic: Shouli succeeded to the princely line; originally named Guangren, he was appointed Groom to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 武后革命，畏疾宗室，而守禮以父得罪，與睿宗諸子閉處宮中十餘年。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu changed the dynasty, she feared and distrusted the imperial clan; Shouli, because his father had offended, together with Ruizong's sons was confined within the palace for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu changed the dynasty, she feared and distrusted the imperial clan; because his father had been disgraced, Shouli was confined within the palace together with Ruizong's sons for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 睿宗封相王，許出外邸，於是守禮等始居外，改司議郎。

translations.literal: Ruizong was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiang and permitted an outer residence; thus Shouli and the others first lived outside and were changed to Director of Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiang and permitted an outer residence, Shouli and the others were at last allowed to live outside the palace and were appointed Directors of Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，復故封，拜光祿卿，實封戶五百。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, his former enfeoffment was restored; he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; actual fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, Shouli's former enfeoffment was restored; he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with an actual fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 唐隆元年，進封邠王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tanglong, he was advanced to Prince of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tanglong, he was promoted to Prince of Bin.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，兼檢校左金吾衛大將軍，出為幽州刺史，遙兼單于大都護，遷司空。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he concurrently served as Acting General-in-Chief of the Left Jinwu Guard; went out as Prefect of Youzhou; remotely concurrently served as Grand Protector-General of the Chanyu Court; transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Shouli concurrently served as Acting General-in-Chief of the Left Jinwu Guard, was sent out as Prefect of Youzhou while remotely serving as Grand Protector-General of the Chanyu Court, and was later transferred to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 開元初，累為州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, he successively served as several prefects.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, he served successively as several prefects.

sentences.zh: 時寧、申、岐、薛王同為刺史，皆擇僚首持綱紀。

translations.literal: At the time the Princes of Ning, Shen, Qi, and Xue all served as prefects; each chose outstanding subordinates to uphold discipline.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Princes of Ning, Shen, Qi, and Xue all served as prefects, and each chose outstanding subordinates to uphold local administration.

sentences.zh: 守禮惟弋獵酣樂，不領事，故源乾曜、袁嘉祚、潘好禮皆為邠府長史、州佐，督檢之。

translations.literal: Shouli only hunted and feasted in pleasure, not attending to affairs; therefore Yuan Qianyao, Yuan Jiazuo, and Pan Haoli all served as Chief Secretaries of the Bin prefecture and prefectural aides, supervising and inspecting him.
translations.idiomatic: Shouli cared only for hunting and feasting and did not attend to affairs, so Yuan Qianyao, Yuan Jiazuo, and Pan Haoli all served as chief secretaries of the Bin prefecture and prefectural aides to supervise him.

sentences.zh: 後還諸王京師，守禮以外支為王，不甚才而多寵嬖，子六十餘人，無可稱者。

translations.literal: Later when the princes returned to the capital, Shouli as a prince of the collateral line was not very talented yet had many favored concubines; more than sixty sons; none worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the princes returned to the capital, Shouli — a prince of the collateral line and not particularly talented — kept many favored concubines and had more than sixty sons, none of whom distinguished themselves.

sentences.zh: 常負息錢數百萬。

translations.literal: He constantly owed interest-bearing debts of several million.
translations.idiomatic: He was constantly in debt for several million in interest-bearing loans.

sentences.zh: 或勸少治居產，守禮曰：「豈天子兄無葬者邪？」

translations.literal: Some urged him to tend his household property a little; Shouli said: "Could the Emperor's elder brother have no one to bury him?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged him to manage his household property, Shouli said, "Could the Emperor's elder brother really lack someone to bury him?"

sentences.zh: 諸王每白上以為歡。

translations.literal: The princes often reported this to the Emperor for his amusement.
translations.idiomatic: The princes often reported this to the Emperor, who found it amusing.

sentences.zh: 岐王嘗奏守禮知雨，暘帝問故，答曰：「臣無它，當天後時，太子被罪，臣幽宮中，歲被敕杖凡四三，累創痕膚，前雨則沈懣，霽則佳，以此知之。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi once memorialized that Shouli could predict rain; in drought the Emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Your subject has nothing else; when Empress Wu was in power, the crown prince was condemned, your subject was confined in the palace, and each year was ordered beaten three or four times; wounds accumulated on his skin; before rain he felt depressed; when clear he felt well; by this he knew."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi once reported that Shouli could predict rain; during a drought the Emperor asked why, and Shouli replied, "I have no special art — when Empress Wu was in power, the crown prince was condemned and I was confined in the palace, beaten on imperial order three or four times a year until my skin was covered with scars; before rain I feel depressed, and when the sky clears I feel well — that is how I know."

sentences.zh: 因泣下，帝為惻然。

translations.literal: He wept; the Emperor was moved to pity.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he spoke, and the Emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 薨，年七十，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died; aged seventy; posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 子承宏、承寧、承寀可記者。

translations.literal: Sons Chenghong, Chengning, and Chengcai are worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: Among his sons, Chenghong, Chengning, and Chengcai are worth noting.

sentences.zh: 承宏，爵廣武王，坐交非其人，貶房州別駕，還為宗正卿。

translations.literal: Chenghong, enfeoffed as Prince of Guangwu; for associating with improper persons, demoted to Vice-Prefect of Fangzhou; returned to serve as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghong was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangwu; for associating with unsuitable men he was demoted to Vice-Prefect of Fangzhou, but later returned to serve as Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，吐蕃入京師，天子如陜，虜宰相馬重英立承宏為帝，以翰林學士於可封、霍瑰為宰相。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde, the Tibetans entered the capital; the Son of Heaven went to Shan; the captive minister Ma Chongying installed Chenghong as emperor; Academicians-in-Attendance Yu Kefeng and Huo Gui were made chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangde, when the Tibetans entered the capital and the Son of Heaven fled to Shan, the captive minister Ma Chongying installed Chenghong as emperor and appointed Academicians-in-Attendance Yu Kefeng and Huo Gui as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 賊退，詔放承宏於華州，死。

translations.literal: When the rebels withdrew, an edict released Chenghong at Huazhou; he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels withdrew, an edict released Chenghong at Huazhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 承寧封嗣邠王。

translations.literal: Chengning was enfeoffed as heir Prince of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Chengning was enfeoffed as heir Prince of Bin.

sentences.zh: 承寀，煌王，拜宗正卿，與仆固懷恩使回紇和親，即納其女為妃，封毘伽公主。

translations.literal: Chengcai, Prince of Huang; appointed Director of the Imperial Clan; with Pugu Huai'en went as envoy to the Uyghurs for a marriage alliance; immediately took their daughter as consort; enfeoffed as Princess Pijia.
translations.idiomatic: Chengcai, Prince of Huang, was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan; he accompanied Pugu Huai'en on a marriage alliance mission to the Uyghurs, took their khan's daughter as his consort, and she was enfeoffed as Princess Pijia.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 唐制：嗣郡王加四品階，親王子服緋。

translations.literal: Tang custom: heirs of commandery princes received four ranks of promotion; sons of imperial princes wore scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang custom, heirs of commandery princes received a four-rank promotion, while sons of imperial princes wore scarlet robes.

sentences.zh: 開元中，張九齡奏：「寧、薛及邠王三子為王者賜紫，餘皆服緋，官不越六局郎，王府掾屬仍員外置。」

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan, Zhang Jiuling memorialized: "The Princes of Ning and Xue and the three sons of the Prince of Bin who held princely titles were granted purple; the rest wore scarlet; offices did not exceed Sixth Bureau Director; princely household staff were still appointed as supernumeraries."
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era, Zhang Jiuling memorialized: "The Princes of Ning and Xue and the three sons of the Prince of Bin who held princely titles were granted purple robes; the rest wore scarlet; their offices did not exceed Sixth Bureau Director, and princely household staff were still appointed as supernumeraries."

sentences.zh: 後從帝至蜀者皆服紫。

translations.literal: Later those who followed the Emperor to Shu all wore purple.
translations.idiomatic: Later, all who followed the Emperor to Shu wore purple.

sentences.zh: 中宗子中宗四子：韋庶人生重潤，後宮生重福、重俊、殤帝。

translations.literal: Sons of Zhongzong — Zhongzong had four sons: Consort Wei bore Chongrun; the rear palace bore Chongfu, Chongjun, and the Short-lived Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Zhongzong — Emperor Zhongzong had four sons: Consort Wei bore Chongrun; ladies of the inner palace bore Chongfu, Chongjun, and the Short-lived Emperor.

sentences.zh: 懿德太子懿德太子重潤，本名重照，避武后諱改焉。

translations.literal: Yide Crown Prince — Crown Prince Chongrun, original name Chongzhao; changed to avoid Empress Wu's taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yide — Prince Chongrun, originally named Chongzhao, changed his name to avoid Empress Wu's taboo.

sentences.zh: 帝為皇太子時，生東宮，高宗喜甚，乳月滿，為大赦天下，改元永淳。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was crown prince, he was born in the Eastern Palace; Gaozong was greatly pleased; when the nursing month was complete, a great amnesty was granted to all under heaven and the era name changed to Yongchun.
translations.idiomatic: While still crown prince, Zhongzong's son was born in the Eastern Palace; Emperor Gaozong was overjoyed, and when the nursing month was complete he granted a great amnesty and changed the era name to Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 是歲，立為皇太孫，開府置官屬。

translations.literal: That year he was installed as imperial grand heir; an office was opened and staff appointed.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was installed as imperial grand heir, with an office opened and staff appointed.

sentences.zh: 帝問吏部侍郎裴敬彜、郎中王方慶，對曰：「禮有嫡子，無嫡孫。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Jingyi and Director Wang Fangqing; they replied: "In ritual there is a designated son but no designated grandson.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Jingyi and Director Wang Fangqing, who replied, "In ritual law there is a designated son but no designated grandson.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏太子在，子但封王。

translations.literal: In Han and Wei, when the crown prince was alive, the son was only enfeoffed as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Han and Wei times, when the crown prince was alive, the son was only enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 晉立湣懷子為皇太孫，齊立文惠子為皇太孫，皆居東宮。

translations.literal: Jin installed Minhuai's son as imperial grand heir; Qi installed Wenhui's son as imperial grand heir; both resided in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jin installed Minhuai's son as imperial grand heir, and Qi installed Wenhui's son as imperial grand heir; both resided in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 今有太子，又立太孫，於古無有。」

translations.literal: Now there is a crown prince, yet an imperial grand heir is also installed; in antiquity there was none."
translations.idiomatic: To have a crown prince and also install an imperial grand heir has no precedent in antiquity."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「自我作古若何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What if I make the precedent myself?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "What if I establish the precedent myself?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「禮，君子抱孫不抱子，孫可以為王父屍者，昭穆同也。

translations.literal: They replied: "In ritual, the gentleman carries the grandson, not the son; a grandson who may stand in for the deceased grandfather — the lineages align.
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "In ritual, a gentleman carries his grandson in his arms rather than his son; a grandson who may represent his deceased grandfather shares the same lineage alignment.

sentences.zh: 陛下肇建皇孫，本支千億之慶。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty first establishes the imperial grand heir; the root branch's blessing of a thousandfold increase."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's establishment of an imperial grand heir brings the blessing of a thousandfold increase to the root branch of the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，詔議官屬。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and ordered discussion of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and ordered deliberation on the staff appointments.

sentences.zh: 敬彜等奏置師、傅、友、文學、祭酒、左右長史、東西曹掾、主簿、管記、司錄、六曹等官，加王府一級，然卒不補。

translations.literal: Jingyi and others memorialized to establish Tutor, Mentor, Companion, Academician, Chancellor, Left and Right Chief Secretaries, East and West Bureau Clerks, Recorder, Archive Keeper, Registrar, Six Bureaus, and other offices, one rank above a princely establishment; yet in the end none were filled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi and others memorialized to establish the offices of Tutor, Mentor, Companion, Academician, Chancellor, Left and Right Chief Secretaries, East and West Bureau Clerks, Recorder, Archive Keeper, Registrar, and the Six Bureaus — one rank above a normal princely establishment — yet in the end none of the posts were filled.

sentences.zh: 將封嵩山，召太子赴東都，以太孫留守京師。

translations.literal: When about to perform the fengshan at Mount Song, the crown prince was summoned to the Eastern Capital; the imperial grand heir was left to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was about to perform the fengshan rite at Mount Song, the crown prince was summoned to the Eastern Capital while the imperial grand heir was left to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 中宗失位，太孫府廢，貶庶人，別囚之。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong lost his position, the grand heir's office was abolished; he was demoted to commoner; separately imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong lost the throne, the grand heir's office was abolished; Chongrun was demoted to commoner status and imprisoned separately.

sentences.zh: 帝復位，封邵王。

translations.literal: When the Emperor regained his position, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor regained the throne, Chongrun was enfeoffed as Prince of Shao.

sentences.zh: 大足中，張易之兄弟得幸武后，或譖重潤與其女弟永泰郡主及主婿竊議，後怒，杖殺之，年十九。

translations.literal: In Dazu, the Zhang Yizhi brothers gained Empress Wu's favor; someone slandered Chongrun, the Princess of Yongtai, and the princess's husband for secret discussions; the Empress was enraged and had him beaten to death; aged nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazu era, the Zhang Yizhi brothers gained Empress Wu's favor; someone slandered Chongrun, the Princess of Yongtai, and the princess's husband for having spoken privately about the Empress; enraged, she had Chongrun beaten to death; he was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 重潤秀容儀，以孝愛稱，誅不緣罪，人皆流涕。

translations.literal: Chongrun had fine countenance and bearing; was known for filial love; execution was not for a crime; all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrun was handsome in bearing and famed for filial devotion; he was killed without cause, and all who heard wept.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追贈皇太子及謚，陪葬乾陵，號墓為陵，贈主為公主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, posthumously made crown prince and given a posthumous title; buried alongside at Qian Mausoleum; the tomb was styled a mausoleum; the princess was posthumously granted princess rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, he was posthumously elevated to crown prince and given a posthumous title, buried alongside Emperor Gaozong at Qian Mausoleum with his tomb styled a mausoleum; the Princess of Yongtai was posthumously granted full princess rank.

sentences.zh: 譙王重福，高宗時王唐昌郡，徙封平恩。

translations.literal: Prince of Qiao — Prince Chongfu; under Gaozong enfeoffed as Prince of Tangchang Commandery; transferred and enfeoffed as Prince of Ping'en.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qiao — Prince Chongfu was under Gaozong enfeoffed as Prince of Tangchang Commandery and later transferred to Prince of Ping'en.

sentences.zh: 長安末乃進王。

translations.literal: At the end of Chang'an he was advanced to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chang'an era he was promoted to full princely rank.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，韋庶人譖與張易之兄弟陷重潤，貶濮州員外刺史，徙合、均二州，不領事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Consort Wei slandered that he together with the Zhang Yizhi brothers had framed Chongrun; demoted to Acting Prefect of Puzhou; transferred to He and Jun prefectures; did not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, Consort Wei slandered that he and the Zhang Yizhi brothers had framed Chongrun; he was demoted to Acting Prefect of Puzhou, then transferred to He and Jun prefectures without actually governing.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，中宗親郊，赦天下，十惡者咸宥，流人得還。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong, Zhongzong personally performed the suburban sacrifice; amnestied all under heaven; the ten abominations were all pardoned; exiles were permitted to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jinglong, Emperor Zhongzong personally performed the suburban sacrifice, amnestied the realm, pardoned even those guilty of the ten abominations, and allowed exiles to return.

sentences.zh: 重福不得歸，自陳「蒼生皆自新，而一子擯棄，皇天平分，固若此乎！」

translations.literal: Chongfu was not permitted to return; he pleaded: "All living people are granted renewal, yet one son is cast aside — is Heaven's justice truly so?"
translations.idiomatic: Chongfu was not permitted to return and pleaded, "All the people are granted renewal, yet one son alone is cast aside — is this truly Heaven's justice?"

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply.
translations.idiomatic: He received no reply.

sentences.zh: 韋后得政，詔左屯衛大將軍趙承恩、薛思簡以兵護守。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei seized power, she ordered Left Tunwei General Zhao Chengen and Xue Sijian to guard him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei seized power, she ordered Left Tunwei General Zhao Chengen and Xue Sijian to guard him under armed escort.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，徙集州，未行，洛陽男子張靈均說重福曰：「大王居嫡長，當為天子。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he was transferred to Jizhou; before departing, a Luoyang man Zhang Lingjun persuaded Chongfu: "Your Highness as eldest legitimate son ought to be Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Chongfu was transferred to Jizhou; before he could depart, a Luoyang man named Zhang Lingjun persuaded him, "Your Highness, as the eldest legitimate son, ought to be Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 相王雖平大難，安可越居大位？

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang though he quelled great disaster — how can he leap over you to occupy the great position?
translations.idiomatic: Though the Prince of Xiang quelled a great crisis, how can he leap over you to take the throne?

sentences.zh: 昔漢誅諸呂，乃東迎代王。

translations.literal: Formerly when Han executed the Lü clan, they then went east to welcome the Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, after the Lü clan was destroyed, the court went east to welcome the Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 今百官士庶皆願王來。

translations.literal: Now the hundred officials and common people all wish Your Highness to come.
translations.idiomatic: Now officials and commoners alike wish for Your Highness to come.

sentences.zh: 王若陰幸東都，殺留守，擁兵西據陜，徇河南、河北，天下可圖也。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness secretly visits the Eastern Capital, kills the regent-in-charge, gathers troops and occupies Shan in the west, and marches through Henan and Hebei, the realm can be seized."
translations.idiomatic: If you slip away to the Eastern Capital in secret, kill the regent there, gather troops and seize Shaan from the west, then sweep through Henan and Hebei, the realm can be yours."

sentences.zh: 重福又遣靈均與其黨鄭愔計，愔亦密招重福為天子，豫尊睿宗為皇季叔，重茂皇太弟，制稱中元克復元年，愔自署左丞相，知內外文武事，以靈均為右丞相、天柱大將軍，知出征事，其餘以次除署。

translations.literal: Chongfu again sent Lingjun to plan with his partisan Zheng Yin. Yin also secretly enlisted Chongfu as Son of Heaven, proposing to honor Ruizong as Imperial Younger Uncle, Chongmao as Imperial Younger Brother, and the era name Zhongyuan Kefu Year One. Yin appointed himself Left Chancellor in charge of civil and military affairs inside and outside; Lingjun as Right Chancellor and Grand General of the Heavenly Pillar in charge of expeditionary affairs; the rest appointed in order.
translations.idiomatic: Chongfu also sent Lingjun to confer with his ally Zheng Yin, who likewise secretly recruited Chongfu as emperor. They planned to honor Ruizong as Imperial Younger Uncle and Chongmao as Imperial Younger Brother, with the reign title Zhongyuan Kefu, Year One. Yin would appoint himself Left Chancellor, overseeing all civil and military affairs; Lingjun would be Right Chancellor and Grand General of the Heavenly Pillar, overseeing campaigns; the rest would receive appointments in turn.

sentences.zh: 重福自均州與靈均乘驛趨東都，舍駙馬裴巽家。

translations.literal: Chongfu from Junzhou joined Lingjun traveling by post horse to rush to the Eastern Capital and lodged at Palace Attendant Pei Xun's house.
translations.idiomatic: Chongfu left Junzhou and rode post horses with Lingjun to rush to Luoyang, staying at the home of Palace Attendant Pei Xun.

sentences.zh: 洛陽令候巽，重福驚，遽出，欲劫左右屯營兵，至天津橋，願從者數百人。

translations.literal: The Luoyang magistrate was watching Pei Xun. Chongfu was alarmed, hurried out, intending to seize the Left and Right Garrison troops. At Tianjin Bridge, only a few hundred wished to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Luoyang was staking out Pei Xun's house. Alarmed, Chongfu fled at once, intending to seize the Left and Right Garrison troops. At Tianjin Bridge, only a few hundred men were willing to follow him.

sentences.zh: 侍御史李邕遇之，先馳至右屯營，呼曰：「譙王得罪先帝，擅入都為亂。

translations.literal: Censor Li Yong encountered him, first galloped to the Right Garrison camp, and shouted: "The Prince of Qiao offended the late Emperor and entered the capital without authorization to make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Yong met him on the way, galloped ahead to the Right Garrison camp, and cried out, "The Prince of Qiao offended the late emperor and has entered the capital without permission to raise rebellion.

sentences.zh: 公等勉立功取富貴。」

translations.literal: Gentlemen, strive to earn merit and obtain wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen, do your utmost to win merit and gain wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 稍稍閉皇城諸門以拒。

translations.literal: Gradually the gates of the Imperial City were closed to refuse him.
translations.idiomatic: One by one the gates of the Imperial City were shut to keep him out.

sentences.zh: 重福徇右營不能動，趨左掖門，已闔，怒，縱火燒之。

translations.literal: Chongfu tried to win over the Right Camp but could not move them. He hastened to the Left Flanking Gate; it was already shut. Angry, he set fire to burn it.
translations.idiomatic: Chongfu tried to rally the Right Camp but could not move them. He rushed to the Left Flanking Gate, but it was already closed. Enraged, he set it ablaze.

sentences.zh: 左營兵寢逼，眾遂潰，重福走山谷。

translations.literal: The Left Camp soldiers pressed close. The crowd then collapsed. Chongfu fled to the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers from the Left Camp closed in, and his followers scattered. Chongfu fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 明日，留守裴談總兵大索，投漕渠死，年三十一，礫其屍。

translations.literal: The next day, regent Pei Tan gathered troops for a great search. He threw himself into the canal and died, age thirty-one. His corpse was reduced to gravel.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Regent Pei Tan mobilized troops for a thorough search. Chongfu drowned himself in the canal. He was thirty-one. His body was pelted with stones.

sentences.zh: 帝詔以三品禮葬。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered burial with third-rank rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that he be buried with third-rank honors.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子節湣太子重俊，聖曆三年王義興，神龍初，王衛，拜洛州牧，實封千戶。

translations.literal: Respectful and Lamented Crown Prince — the Respectful and Lamented Crown Prince Chongjun. In the third year of Shengli he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yixing; at the beginning of Shenlong as Prince of Wei; appointed Governor of Luozhou; actual fief one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Respectful and Lamented Crown Prince Chongjun was enfeoffed as Prince of Yixing in the third year of Shengli. At the start of the Shenlong era he was made Prince of Wei and appointed Governor of Luozhou, with an actual fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 俄領揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Soon after he also held the post of Grand Commander of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was also made Grand Commander of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年為皇太子，與太后喪，殺冊禮，詔在籓食封，歲納東宮。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Crown Prince. When the Empress Dowager died, accession rites were curtailed. An edict said he would receive fief income while at his princely domain, paying tribute yearly to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made crown prince. When the empress dowager died, the enthronement ceremony was scaled back. An edict allowed him to draw income from his fief while at his princely estate and to pay an annual tribute to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 給事中盧粲上言：「太子與列國同入封，不可為法。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Lu Can submitted: "The Crown Prince receiving fief income like the feudal princes — this cannot serve as precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Lu Can submitted a memorial: "For the crown prince to draw fief income like the feudal princes cannot be made precedent."

sentences.zh: 詔罷之。

translations.literal: An edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put an end to the practice.

sentences.zh: 重俊性明果，然少法度。

translations.literal: Chongjun was bright and resolute by nature, yet lacked regulation in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjun was bright and resolute by nature, but he had little sense of propriety.

sentences.zh: 既楊璬、武崇訓為賓客，二人馮貴寵，無學術，惟狗馬蹴踘相戲昵。

translations.literal: Once Yang Rui and Wu Chongxun became his clients, the two men relied on noble favor, had no learning, and only played with dogs, horses, and cuju football, treating each other intimately in jest.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Rui and Wu Chongxun became his companions, the two men traded on their lofty connections. They had no learning and spent their days with dogs, horses, and cuju, amusing themselves together.

sentences.zh: 左庶子姚珽數上疏諍導，右庶子平貞慎又獻《孝經議》、《養德》等傳，太子納而不克用。

translations.literal: Left Junior Mentor Yao Ting repeatedly submitted memorials admonishing and guiding; Right Junior Mentor Ping Zhenshen also presented "Discourse on the Classic of Filial Piety," "Nourishing Virtue," and other treatises. The Crown Prince accepted them but could not fully apply them.
translations.idiomatic: Left Junior Mentor Yao Ting repeatedly submitted memorials to admonish and guide him. Right Junior Mentor Ping Zhenshen also presented treatises such as Discourse on the Classic of Filial Piety and Nourishing Virtue. The crown prince accepted them but could not bring himself to follow them.

sentences.zh: 武三思挾韋后勢，將圖逆，內忌太子，而崇訓又三思子，尚安樂公主，常教主辱重俊，以非韋出，詈為奴，數請廢，自為皇太女。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi relied on Empress Wei's power, was plotting treason, and inwardly resented the Crown Prince. Moreover Chongxun was Sansi's son, married to Princess Anle. She often taught her husband to humiliate Chongjun — that he was not born of the Wei clan, reviled him as a slave, repeatedly petitioned for his deposition, and sought to become Imperial Grand Princess herself.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi, leaning on Empress Wei's power, was plotting rebellion and inwardly resented the crown prince. Chongxun was Sansi's son and husband to Princess Anle. She often urged her husband to humiliate Chongjun, calling him a bastard of non-Wei birth and reviling him as a slave. She repeatedly petitioned to have him deposed so that she herself might become crown princess.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，重俊恚忿，遂率李多祚洎左羽林將軍李思沖、李承況、獨孤祎之、沙咤忠義，矯發左羽林及千騎兵殺三思、崇訓並其黨十餘人，使左金吾大將軍成王千里守宮城，自率兵趨肅章門，斬關入，索韋后、安樂公主、昭容上官所在。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, Chongjun, burning with resentment, then led Li Duozuo together with Left Yulin General Li Sichong, Li Chengkuang, Dugu Yizhi, and Shazha Zhongyi, falsely issuing orders to mobilize the Left Yulin and thousand-rider troops to kill Sansi, Chongxun, and more than ten of their partisans.
