He sent Left Jinwu Grand General Prince Cheng Wang Qianli to guard the palace city; he himself led troops to Su Zhang Gate, cut through the barrier and entered, searching for Empress Wei, Princess Anle, and Lady Shangguan the Brilliant Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year, burning with rage, Chongjun led Li Duozuo and the Left Yulin generals Li Sichong, Li Chengkuang, Dugu Yizhi, and Shazha Zhongyi. Under false orders they mobilized the Left Yulin Guard and the thousand-rider corps, killed Sansi, Chongxun, and more than ten of their followers, and sent Left Jinwu Grand General Prince Cheng Wang Qianli to hold the palace city. Chongjun himself led troops to Su Zhang Gate, broke through the gate, and searched for Empress Wei, Princess Anle, and Brilliant Attendant Lady Shangguan.

sentences.zh: 後挾帝升玄武門，宰相楊再思、蘇瑰、李嶠及宗楚客、紀處訥統兵二千餘人守太極殿，帝召右羽林將軍劉仁景等率留軍飛騎百人拒之，多祚兵不得進。

translations.literal: Later he forced the Emperor up the Xuanwu Gate. Chancellors Yang Zaisi, Su Gui, Li Qiao, and Zong Chuke and Ji Chuna commanded over two thousand troops guarding the Hall of Supreme Ultimate. The Emperor summoned Right Yulin General Liu Renjing and others to lead a hundred flying cavalry of the remaining guard to resist; Duozuo's troops could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He then forced the emperor up to the Xuanwu Gate. Chancellors Yang Zaisi, Su Gui, and Li Qiao, together with Zong Chuke and Ji Chuna, mustered more than two thousand men to guard the Hall of Supreme Ultimate. The emperor summoned Right Yulin General Liu Renjing and others to lead a hundred flying cavalry from the palace guard against them, and Duozuo's troops could not advance.

sentences.zh: 帝據檻語千騎曰：「爾乃我爪牙，何忽為亂？

translations.literal: The Emperor leaned on the railing and addressed the thousand-riders: "You are my claws and teeth — why suddenly rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Leaning on the railing, the emperor addressed the thousand-riders: "You are my own claws and teeth — why have you suddenly turned to rebellion?

sentences.zh: 能斬賊者有賞。」

translations.literal: Whoever can behead the rebels will be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever cuts down the rebels will be rewarded."

sentences.zh: 於是士倒戈斬多祚，余黨潰。

translations.literal: At this the soldiers turned their swords and beheaded Duozuo; the remaining partisans collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: At that the troops turned on Duozuo and killed him; the rest of the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 重俊亡入終南山，欲奔突厥，楚客遣果毅趙思慎追之，重俊憩於野，為左右所殺。

translations.literal: Chongjun fled into Zhongnan Mountains, intending to flee to the Turks. Chuke sent Colonel Zhao Shenshen in pursuit. Chongjun rested in the wild and was killed by his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjun fled into the Zhongnan Mountains, intending to escape to the Turks. Chuke sent Colonel Zhao Shenshen in pursuit. Resting in the wilderness, Chongjun was killed by his own followers.

sentences.zh: 詔殊首朝堂，獻太廟，並以告三思、崇訓柩。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his head severed and displayed at court, presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and also announced at the coffins of Sansi and Chongxun.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his head cut off and displayed at court, offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and reported to the coffins of Sansi and Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，加贈謚，陪葬定陵。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, posthumous titles and burial honors were added; he was buried with Ding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, posthumous honors were added and Chongjun was buried beside Ding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 初，重俊被害，官屬莫敢視，惟永和丞寧嘉勖號哭，解衣裹其首，時人義之；

translations.literal: At first when Chongjun was killed, his officials and staff dared not look. Only Yonghe Assistant Magistrate Ning Jiaxu wailed loudly, removed his garment to wrap the head. People of the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongjun was killed, none of his staff dared even to look at his body. Only Yonghe Assistant Magistrate Ning Jiaxu wailed aloud, stripped off his own garment, and wrapped the prince's head. People of the time honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 楚客怒，收付獄，貶平興丞，卒。

translations.literal: Chuke was angry, had him arrested and imprisoned, demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Pingxing, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke was enraged, had him arrested and thrown into prison, and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Pingxing, where he died.

sentences.zh: 至是，亦贈永和令。

translations.literal: At this time, he was also posthumously granted the title Magistrate of Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ning was also posthumously granted the title of magistrate of Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 重俊子宗暉，景雲三年封湖陽郡王，天寶中，至太常員外卿，薨。

translations.literal: Chongjun's son Zonghui — in the third year of Jingyun enfeoffed as Prince of Huyang Commandery; during Tianbao reached Supernumerary Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; died.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjun's son Zonghui was enfeoffed as Prince of Huyang Commandery in the third year of Jingyun. During the Tianbao era he rose to supernumerary director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and then died.

sentences.zh: 睿宗子睿宗六子：肅明皇后生憲，宮人柳生捴，昭成皇后生玄宗皇帝，崔孺人生範，王德妃生業，後宮生隆悌。

translations.literal: Ruizong's sons: Ruizong had six sons — Empress Suming bore Xian; palace woman Liu bore Cui; Empress Zhaocheng bore Emperor Xuanzong; Lady Cui the Commoner bore Fan; Consort Wang De bore Ye; a rear palace woman bore Longti.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong had six sons: Empress Suming bore Xian; the palace woman Liu bore Cui; Empress Zhaocheng bore Emperor Xuanzong; Lady Cui the Commoner bore Fan; Consort Wang De bore Ye; and a woman of the inner palace bore Longti.

sentences.zh: 讓皇帝憲，始王永平。

translations.literal: The Yielding Emperor Xian — initially Prince of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: The Yielding Emperor Xian was at first Prince of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 文明元年，武后以睿宗為皇帝，故憲立為皇太子；

translations.literal: In the first year of Wenming, Wu made Ruizong Emperor, so Xian was established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wenming, when Empress Wu made Ruizong emperor, Xian was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 睿宗降為皇嗣，更冊為皇孫，與諸王皆出閤，開府置官屬。

translations.literal: Ruizong was reduced to Imperial Heir, then re-enfeoffed as Imperial Grandson; together with the princes all left the inner apartments, opened offices and established staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong was reduced to imperial heir and then re-enfeoffed as imperial grandson, Xian and the other princes all left the inner quarters, opened princely offices, and appointed staffs.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，降王壽春，與衡陽、巴陵、彭城三王同封，復詔入閤。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou, reduced to Prince of Shouchun; together with the princes of Hengyang, Baling, and Pengcheng enfeoffed at the same time; again ordered to enter the inner apartments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou he was reduced to Prince of Shouchun and enfeoffed at the same time as the princes of Hengyang, Baling, and Pengcheng; he was again ordered into the inner apartments.

sentences.zh: 中宗立，改王蔡，固辭不敢當。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, changed to Prince of Cai; firmly declined, daring not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, Xian was made Prince of Cai, but he firmly declined and refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 唐隆元年，進封宋。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tanglong, advanced to Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tanglong he was advanced to Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 睿宗將建東宮，以憲嫡長，又嘗為太子，而楚王有大功，故久不定。

translations.literal: When Ruizong was about to establish the Eastern Palace — because Xian was eldest legitimate son and had once been Crown Prince, yet the Prince of Chu had great merit — for a long time it was undecided.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong was about to establish the Eastern Palace, the choice remained unsettled for a long time: Xian was the eldest legitimate son and had once been crown prince, but the Prince of Chu had rendered great service.

sentences.zh: 憲辭曰：「儲副，天下公器，時平則先嫡，國難則先功，重社稷也。

translations.literal: Xian declined, saying: "The heir apparent is the public vessel of the realm. In peaceful times the eldest legitimate son comes first; in national crisis merit comes first — prioritizing the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Xian declined, saying, "The heir apparent is the common trust of the realm. In peaceful times precedence goes to the eldest legitimate son; in times of crisis precedence goes to merit — because the altars of state come first.

sentences.zh: 使付授非宜，海內失望，臣以死請。」

translations.literal: If the transfer is inappropriate, the realm within the seas will lose hope. Your subject requests this with his life."
translations.idiomatic: If the succession is wrongly assigned, the empire will lose heart. I beg this at the cost of my life."

sentences.zh: 因涕泣固讓。

translations.literal: He wept and firmly yielded.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he pressed his refusal.

sentences.zh: 時大臣亦言楚王有定社稷功，且聖庶抗嫡，不宜更議。

translations.literal: At the time great ministers also said the Prince of Chu had merit in stabilizing the altars, and moreover a sage's illegitimate son resisting the legitimate heir — it was inappropriate to reconsider further.
translations.idiomatic: The leading ministers also argued that the Prince of Chu had saved the dynasty, and that a sage emperor's favored younger son should not be set aside for the eldest legitimate heir; further debate was out of place.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉憲讓，遂許之，立楚王為皇太子，以憲為雍州牧、揚州大都督、太子太師，實封至二千戶，賜甲第，物段五千，良馬二十，奴婢十房，上田三十頃。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised Xian's yielding and consented. Established the Prince of Chu as Crown Prince. Appointed Xian Governor of Yongzhou, Grand Commander of Yangzhou, Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince; actual fief reaching two thousand households; granted a fine mansion, five thousand bolts of goods, twenty fine horses, ten households of slaves, thirty qing of superior fields.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Xian's selflessness and agreed. The Prince of Chu was made crown prince. Xian was appointed Governor of Yongzhou, Grand Commander of Yangzhou, and Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince, with an actual fief of two thousand households. He was also granted a fine mansion, five thousand bolts of goods, twenty fine horses, ten households of slaves, and thirty qing of superior farmland.

sentences.zh: 進尚書左僕射，又兼司徒。

translations.literal: Advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; also concurrently Situ.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and also made Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 讓司徒，更為太子賓客。

translations.literal: He yielded the post of Situ and was made instead a Client of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post of Minister over the Masses and was instead made a client of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時太平公主有醜圖，姚元崇、宋璟白帝，請出憲及申王成義為刺史，以銷釋陰計，乃以司徒兼蒲州刺史，進司空。

translations.literal: At the time Princess Taiping had ugly designs. Yao Chongyuan and Song Jing informed the Emperor, requesting that Xian and the Prince of Shen Cheng Wang Chengyi be sent out as regional governors to dissolve covert schemes. He was then made Situ concurrently Governor of Puzhou; advanced to Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Princess Taiping was plotting treacherously. Yao Chongyuan and Song Jing reported this to the emperor and asked that Xian and Prince Shen Wang Chengyi be sent out as regional governors to break up her secret designs. Xian was then made Minister over the Masses and concurrently Governor of Puzhou, and promoted to Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 玄宗既討定蕭、岑之難，進憲位太尉，贈千戶，固辭，更授開府儀同三司，解太尉、揚州大都督。

translations.literal: After Xuanzong had suppressed the crisis of Xiao and Cen, Xian's rank was advanced to Grand General; added one thousand households to his fief; he firmly declined. Instead granted Grand Precedence with the Honor of Three Excellencies; relieved of Grand General and Grand Commander of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanzong had put down the crisis involving Xiao and Cen, Xian was promoted to Grand General and granted an additional thousand households, but he firmly declined. He was instead given the honor of Grand Precedence Equal to the Three Excellencies and relieved of the posts of Grand General and Grand Commander of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙王寧，又兼太常卿。

translations.literal: Transferred to Prince of Ning; also concurrently Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prince of Ning and also made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 開元十四年，表解卿。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan, memorialized to resign the directorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan he submitted a memorial asking to resign the directorship.

sentences.zh: 久之，復為太尉。

translations.literal: After a long time, again made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was again made Grand General.

sentences.zh: 歷澤、岐、涇三州刺史，累封至五千五百戶。

translations.literal: Successively served as governor of Ze, Qi, and Jing prefectures; cumulative fief reached five thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Ze, Qi, and Jing prefectures, and his cumulative fief rose to five thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二十九年薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-ninth year of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，帝五子列第東都積善坊，號「五王子宅」。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor's five sons had mansions arranged in Jishan Ward of the Eastern Capital, called "the Five Princes' Residence."
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor's five sons had their mansions lined up in Jishan Ward of Luoyang, called "the Five Princes' Residence."

sentences.zh: 及賜第上都隆慶坊，亦號「五王宅」。

translations.literal: When granted mansions in Longqing Ward of the upper capital, they were also called "the Five Princes' Mansion."
translations.idiomatic: When mansions were granted in Longqing Ward of the capital, they were likewise called "the Five Princes' Mansion."

sentences.zh: 玄宗為太子，嘗制大衾長枕，將與諸王共之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was Crown Prince, he once made a large quilt and long pillow, intending to share them with the princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong was crown prince, he once had a large quilt and long pillow made, intending to share them with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 睿宗知，喜甚。

translations.literal: Ruizong learned of it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong heard of this and was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 及先天後，盡以隆慶舊邸為興慶宮，而賜憲及薛王第於勝業坊，申、岐二王居安興坊，環列宮側。

translations.literal: After the Xiantian era, all the old Longqing residences were made into Xingqing Palace. Mansions were granted to Xian and the Prince of Xue in Shengye Ward; the Princes of Shen and Qi lived in Anxing Ward, ringing the palace on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiantian era the old Longqing residences were all converted into Xingqing Palace. Mansions in Shengye Ward were granted to Xian and the Prince of Xue, while the princes of Shen and Qi lived in Anxing Ward, encircling the palace.

sentences.zh: 天子於宮西、南置樓，其西署曰「花萼相輝之樓」，南曰「勤政務本之樓」，帝時時登之，聞諸王作樂，必亟召升樓，與同榻坐，或就幸第，賦詩燕嬉，賜金帛侑歡。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven erected towers west and south of the palace. The western was named "Tower of Flowers and Calyxes Shining Upon Each Other"; the southern "Tower of Diligent Governance and Foundational Duty." The Emperor often ascended them. When he heard the princes making music, he always quickly summoned them to ascend the tower, sat on the same couch with them, or personally visited their mansions — composing poetry and feasting in pleasure, bestowing gold and silk to aid their merriment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built towers west and south of the palace: the western tower was named "the Tower of Flowers and Calyxes Shining Upon Each Other," and the southern "the Tower of Diligent Governance and Foundational Duty." He often climbed them. Whenever he heard his brothers making music, he would summon them at once to join him on the tower and sit with them on the same couch, or visit their mansions himself to compose poetry, feast, and give them gold and silk to share in their pleasure.

sentences.zh: 諸王日朝側門，既歸，即具樂縱飲，擊球、鬥雞、馳鷹犬為樂，如是歲月不絕，所至輒中使勞賜相踵，世謂天子友悌，古無有者。

translations.literal: The princes daily attended court at the side gate. Upon returning, they immediately prepared music and drank freely — playing ball games, cockfighting, running hawks and hounds for pleasure. Thus months and years without cease. Wherever they went, palace envoys bearing imperial gifts followed in succession. The age called the Son of Heaven's brotherly affection something the ancients never had.
translations.idiomatic: The princes attended court daily at the side gate. After returning home they would at once set out music and drink freely, playing ball games, cockfighting, and hunting with hawks and hounds. Month after month this never stopped, and wherever they went palace envoys bearing imperial gifts followed one after another. People of the age said the emperor's brotherly affection was unmatched even in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 帝於敦睦蓋天性然，雖讒邪亂其間，而卒無以搖。

translations.literal: The Emperor's harmonious affection was indeed by nature; though slander and wickedness stirred among them, in the end nothing could shake it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's brotherly warmth was truly in his nature; though slander and malice stirred between them, in the end nothing could shake it.

sentences.zh: 時有鶺鴒千數集麟德殿廷樹，翔棲浹日。

translations.literal: At the time several thousand wagtails gathered on the court trees of Linde Hall, flying and roosting for a full day.
translations.idiomatic: At the time several thousand wagtails gathered in the court trees of Linde Hall, flying and roosting there for a whole day.

sentences.zh: 左清道率府長史魏光乘作頌，以為天子友悌之祥。

translations.literal: Left Qingdao Commandant Chief Clerk Wei Guangsheng composed an encomium, taking it as an auspice of the Son of Heaven's brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guangsheng, chief clerk of the Left Qingdao Commandant's office, composed an encomium, taking it as an omen of the emperor's brotherly harmony.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，亦為作頌。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and also composed an encomium.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and composed an encomium of his own.

sentences.zh: 憲尤謹畏，未嘗幹政而與人交，帝益信重，嘗以書賜憲等曰：「魏文帝詩：『西山一何高，高高殊無極。

translations.literal: Xian was especially cautious and reverent, never meddling in government yet associating with people. The Emperor trusted and valued him all the more. He once sent a letter to Xian and the others, saying: "Emperor Wen of Wei's poem: 'How high the western mountains — so high there is no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was especially cautious and restrained. He never meddled in affairs of state, yet he kept close ties with others, and the emperor trusted and valued him all the more. Once he sent a letter to Xian and the others, saying, "In Emperor Wen of Wei's poem: 'How high the western mountains — so high there is no end.

sentences.zh: 上有兩仟童，不飲亦不食。

translations.literal: Above them two thousand youths — neither drinking nor eating.
translations.idiomatic: On them live two thousand youths who neither drink nor eat.

sentences.zh: 賜我一丸藥，光耀有五色。

translations.literal: They gave me one pill of medicine, radiantly possessing five colors.
translations.idiomatic: They gave me one pill of medicine, shining with five colors.

sentences.zh: 服之四五日，身體生羽翼。』

translations.literal: After taking it four or five days, the body sprouts wings.
translations.idiomatic: After taking it for four or five days, the body grows wings.'

sentences.zh: 朕每言服藥而求羽翼，寧如兄弟天生之羽翼乎？

translations.literal: I often say: taking medicine to seek wings — is that not as good as the wings that brothers have by nature?
translations.idiomatic: I often say: to take medicine in search of wings — how can that compare with the wings brothers are born with?

sentences.zh: 陳思王之才，足以經國，絕其朝謁，卒使憂死，魏祚未終，司馬氏奪之，豈神丸效耶？

translations.literal: Prince Si of Chen's talent was sufficient to govern the state. Cao Pi cut off his court audiences; in the end he was worried to death. Wei's mandate was not yet ended when the Sima clan seized it — was that the effect of the divine pill?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Si of Chen had talent enough to govern the state, yet Cao Pi cut off his access to court and in the end worried him to death. Wei's mandate had not yet run its course when the Sima clan seized power — was that the work of a divine pill?

sentences.zh: 虞舜至聖，舍象傲以親九族，九族既睦，平章百姓。

translations.literal: Yu Shun the most sage — put aside his arrogant brother Xiang to draw the nine clans close. Once the nine clans were harmonious, he harmonized and made bright the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shun, the most sage of men, set aside his arrogant brother Xiang to draw the nine clans close. Once the nine clans were at peace, he brought harmony to the common people.

sentences.zh: 今數千載，天下歸善焉，此朕廢寢忘食所慕嘆也。

translations.literal: Now after several thousand years, the realm returns to goodness — this is what I forego sleep and forget meals to admire and sigh over.
translations.idiomatic: Even after thousands of years, the world still honors his goodness — this is what I admire so deeply that I forget sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 頃因余暇，選仟錄得神方，雲餌之必壽。

translations.literal: Recently during spare leisure, having selected and transcribed thousand records, I obtained a divine formula said to guarantee longevity if consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, in a moment of leisure, I copied out a thousand prescriptions and came upon a divine formula said to grant long life if taken.

sentences.zh: 今持此藥，願與兄弟共之，偕至長齡，永永無極也。」

translations.literal: Now holding this medicine, I wish to share it with my brothers, arriving together at long life, forever without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I hold this medicine, I wish to share it with my brothers so that we may all live long together, forever without end."

sentences.zh: 後申王等相繼薨，唯憲在，帝親待愈益厚。

translations.literal: Later the Prince of Shen and others died in succession; only Xian remained. The Emperor's personal regard grew ever more generous.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Prince of Shen and the others died one after another, and only Xian remained. The emperor treated him with ever greater personal affection.

sentences.zh: 每生日必幸其第為壽，往往留宿；

translations.literal: Every birthday he always visited his mansion to celebrate longevity; often stayed overnight.
translations.idiomatic: On every birthday the emperor visited his mansion to celebrate with him, and often stayed the night.

sentences.zh: 居常無日不賜遺，尚食總監及四方所獻酒酪異饌；

translations.literal: Ordinarily not a day passed without bestowals — from the Director-General of the Imperial Kitchen and delicacies and exotic foods presented from the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: On ordinary days there was scarcely a day without gifts — delicacies from the Director-General of the Imperial Kitchen and rare foods sent from all quarters.

sentences.zh: 皆分餉之。

translations.literal: All were divided and sent to him.
translations.idiomatic: All of these were divided and sent to him.

sentences.zh: 憲嘗請歲盡錄賜目付史官，必數百紙。

translations.literal: Xian once requested that at year's end the list of bestowals be recorded and given to the historiographers — inevitably several hundred sheets.
translations.idiomatic: Xian once asked that at year's end the record of gifts be copied out for the historiographers — invariably several hundred pages long.

sentences.zh: 後有疾，護醫將膳，騎相望也。

translations.literal: Later when ill, physicians and food-bearers in attendance lined the roads one after another on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: When he later fell ill, physicians and food-bearers sent from court followed one another on horseback along the road.

sentences.zh: 僧崇一者療之，少損，帝喜甚，賜緋袍、銀魚。

translations.literal: The monk Chongyi treated him; the illness slightly reduced. The Emperor was greatly pleased and granted a crimson robe and silver fish badge.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Chongyi treated him, and his illness eased somewhat. The emperor was overjoyed and granted Chongyi a crimson robe and silver fish badge.

sentences.zh: 已而疾寢劇，薨，年六十三。

translations.literal: Before long the illness grew severe; he died, age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the illness worsened, and he died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 帝失聲號慟，左右皆泣下。

translations.literal: The Emperor cried out in loud grief; those around him all wept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor broke into loud mourning, and those around him all wept.

sentences.zh: 帝以憲實推天下，有高世之行，非大號不稱，乃追謚讓皇帝，遣尚書左丞相裴耀卿、太常卿韋縚持節奉冊。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Xian had truly yielded the realm and had conduct surpassing the age, felt no lesser title would suffice. He posthumously ennobled him the Yielding Emperor and dispatched Left Director of the Department of State Affairs Pei Yaoqing and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Tao bearing credentials to present the encomium.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xian had truly yielded the throne and lived on a level above his age, the emperor felt that no lesser title would suffice. He posthumously honored him as the Yielding Emperor and sent Left Director Pei Yaoqing and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Tao with credentials to present the encomium.

sentences.zh: 其子璡表陳憲宿素退讓，不敢當大號。

translations.literal: His son Jin submitted a memorial stating Xian's lifelong plain modesty and yielding, daring not accept the great title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin submitted a memorial saying that Xian had always been plain and self-effacing and would not have dared accept so great a title.

sentences.zh: 制不許。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict refused the request.

sentences.zh: 及斂，出天子服一稱，詔右監門大將軍高力士以手書寘靈坐，贈妃元為恭皇后，葬橋陵旁。

translations.literal: At the encoffining, one set of the Son of Heaven's robes was produced. An edict ordered Right Palace Gate Grand General Gao Lishi to place a personal letter at the spirit seat. Consort Fei Yuan was posthumously made Empress Gong. Buried beside Qiao Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: At the encoffining a set of imperial robes was brought out. An edict ordered Right Palace Gate Grand General Gao Lishi to place a letter written in the emperor's own hand at the spirit seat. Consort Fei Yuan was posthumously made Empress Gong, and Xian was buried beside Qiao Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 及葬，敕中使諭璡等，送終之具，使眾見之，示以儉薄。

translations.literal: At the burial, palace envoys were commanded to instruct Jin and the others regarding funeral provisions, displaying them to the crowd to show frugality.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial, palace envoys were sent to tell Jin and the others what was being provided for the funeral, showing the items publicly to demonstrate its simplicity.

sentences.zh: 所司請如諸陵，設千味食內壙中，監護使耀卿建言：「尚食料水陸千餘種及馬、牛、驢、犢、麞、鹿、鵝、鴨、魚、雁體節之味，並藥酒三十名，盛夏胎養，不可多殺，考求禮據，無所憑依。

translations.literal: The responsible office requested as at other imperial tombs to set out a thousand-flavor meal inside the burial chamber. Overseer Yaoqing submitted: "The Imperial Kitchen lists over a thousand land and water items — horse, ox, donkey, calf, roe deer, deer, goose, duck, fish, and wild goose in cuts — and thirty kinds of medicinal wine. In midsummer when creatures nurture their young, one cannot slaughter excessively. Examining ritual precedent, there is nothing to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office asked, as at other imperial tombs, to place a thousand-flavor offering inside the burial chamber. Overseer Yaoqing submitted a memorial: "The Imperial Kitchen lists more than a thousand land and water dishes — horse, ox, donkey, calf, roe deer, deer, goose, duck, fish, and wild goose in cuts — along with thirty kinds of medicinal wine. In midsummer, when animals are nursing their young, one should not slaughter so many. I have searched the ritual precedents and found no basis for this.

sentences.zh: 陛下每申讓帝之志，務存約素，請蠲省折衷。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty always declares the Yielding Emperor's intent, striving to preserve simplicity — I request reduction and a balanced compromise."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has repeatedly affirmed the Yielding Emperor's wish to keep things plain and simple. I ask that the offerings be cut back to a balanced minimum."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 既發引，大雨，有詔慶王潭等涉塗泥，步送十里，號其墓曰惠陵。

translations.literal: Once the procession departed, great rain fell. An edict ordered Prince Qing Wang Tan and others to wade through mud and escort on foot for ten li. The tomb was named Huiling (Benevolent Mausoleum).
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession set out, heavy rain fell. An edict ordered Prince Qing Wang Tan and the others to wade through the mud and escort the coffin on foot for ten li. The tomb was named Huiling, the Benevolent Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 憲嘗從帝按舞萬歲樓，帝從復道上見衛士已食，棄其餘竇中。

translations.literal: Xian once followed the Emperor reviewing dancers at Wansui Tower. The Emperor from the elevated passage saw guards who had already eaten discarding the leftovers in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: Xian once accompanied the emperor to watch dancers at Wansui Tower. From the elevated passage the emperor saw guards who had already eaten throwing the leftovers into a ditch.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詔高力士杖殺之，憲從容曰：「從復道上窺人之私，恐士不自安，且失大體，豈以性命輕於余饗乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and ordered Gao Lishi to beat them to death. Xian calmly said: "From the elevated passage to peep at people's private matters — I fear the guards will not feel secure, and moreover it loses great propriety. Can one lightly value lives below leftover food?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and ordered Gao Lishi to beat them to death. Xian said calmly, "To spy on men's private affairs from the elevated passage will make the guards uneasy and, more importantly, violates proper dignity. Can a man's life weigh less than leftover food?"

sentences.zh: 帝遽止，謂力士曰：「王於我，可謂有急難也。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately stopped and said to Lishi: "The Prince to me may be said to have helped in urgent difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stopped him at once and said to Lishi, "The prince has just saved me in a moment of crisis.

sentences.zh: 不然，且誤殺士。」

translations.literal: Otherwise I would almost have wrongly killed the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I would nearly have killed these men by mistake."

sentences.zh: 又涼州獻新曲，帝御便坐，召諸王觀之。

translations.literal: Also, Liangzhou presented a new tune. The Emperor sat informally and summoned the princes to watch.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion Liangzhou presented a new tune. The emperor took an informal seat and summoned the princes to listen.

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「曲雖佳，然宮離而不屬，商亂而暴，君卑逼下，臣僭犯上。

translations.literal: Xian said: "Though the tune is fine, yet the gong mode is detached and not connected; the shang mode is chaotic and violent — the ruler humble pressing the subject below, ministers presumptuous violating those above.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "The tune is fine, but the gong mode is disconnected and unresolved, and the shang mode is chaotic and harsh — as if the ruler were abasing himself and pressing down on his subjects while ministers presumptuously violated their superiors.

sentences.zh: 發於忽微，形於音聲，播之詠歌，見於人事，臣恐一日有播遷之禍。」

translations.literal: Arising from the subtle, taking form in sound, spreading in song and praise, appearing in human affairs — your subject fears that one day there will be the calamity of exile and displacement."
translations.idiomatic: What begins in something slight takes shape in sound, spreads through song, and appears in human affairs. I fear that one day this will bring the calamity of exile and upheaval."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 及安、史亂，世乃思憲審音云。

translations.literal: When the An and Shi rebellion arose, the world then remembered Xian's discernment in music, they say.
translations.idiomatic: When the An-Shi rebellion broke out, people at last recalled what Xian had said about reading music—and how right he had been.

sentences.zh: 憲本名成器，避昭成太后謚，與申王成義俱改今名。

translations.literal: Xian's original name was Chengqi. To avoid the posthumous title of Empress Zhaocheng, he and Prince Shen Cheng Yi both changed to their present names.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had originally been named Chengqi. To avoid the posthumous name of Empress Zhaocheng, he and Prince Shen Cheng Yi both took their present names.

sentences.zh: 憲子十九人，其聞者璡、嗣莊、琳、瑀。

translations.literal: Xian had nineteen sons; among those known were Jin, Sizhuang, Lin, and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had nineteen sons; the best known were Jin, Sizhuang, Lin, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 璡、嗣莊、琳、瑀。

translations.literal: Jin, Sizhuang, Lin, and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, Sizhuang, Lin, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 璡眉宇秀整，性謹絜，善射，帝愛之。

translations.literal: Jin had handsome, refined features; his nature was careful and pure; he was skilled at archery; the Emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had handsome, well-set features, a careful and upright nature, and skill at archery. The emperor loved him.

sentences.zh: 封汝陽王，歷太僕卿。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Ruyang and served as Grand Master of the Household for Horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Prince of Ruyang and served as Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 與賀知章、褚庭誨、梁涉等善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with He Zhizhang, Chu Tinghui, Liang She, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to He Zhizhang, Chu Tinghui, Liang She, and others.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 嗣莊幼有令名，為太子諭德，封濟陰王。

translations.literal: Sizhuang had a fine reputation from youth; he served as Mentor to the Crown Prince and was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhuang had a fine name from childhood. He served as Mentor to the Crown Prince and was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈幽州大都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Grand Protector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made Grand Protector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 琳以秘書監為嗣寧王，從天子幸蜀，薨。

translations.literal: Lin, as Director of the Secretariat, succeeded as Prince of Suining; he followed the Son of Heaven to Shu and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, while serving as Director of the Secretariat, was made Heir Prince of Suining. He followed the emperor into exile in Shu and died there.

sentences.zh: 瑀早有材望，偉儀觀。

translations.literal: Yu from early on had talent and reputation, with a grand presence.
translations.idiomatic: Yu showed early promise and a commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 始封隴西郡公。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 從帝幸蜀，至河池，封漢中王，山南西道防禦使。

translations.literal: Following the Emperor to Shu, at Hechi he was enfeoffed as Prince of Hanzhong and made Military Commissioner of the Western Circuit of Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: On the flight to Shu, he was enfeoffed at Hechi as Prince of Hanzhong and appointed Military Commissioner of the Western Circuit of Shannan.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，寧國公主降回紇，詔瑀以特進、太常卿持節冊拜回紇為威遠可汗。

translations.literal: At the start of the Qianyuan era, when Princess Ningguo was sent in marriage to the Uyghurs, Yu was ordered as Special Promotion Grand Master and Minister of Rites to carry the seal and invest the Uyghur khan as Khan Weiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qianyuan era, when Princess Ningguo was sent to marry the Uyghurs, Yu was ordered, as Special Promotion Grand Master and Minister of Rites, to carry the imperial seal and invest the Uyghur khan as Khan Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 瑀亦知音，嘗早朝過永興裏，聞笛音，顧左右曰：「是太常工乎？」

translations.literal: Yu also understood music. Once on an early morning court session passing Yongxing Lane, he heard flute music and turned to his attendants, saying: "Is that a musician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu also had an ear for music. Once, on his way to early court through Yongxing Lane, he heard a flute and turned to his attendants, saying, "Is that a musician from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices?"

translations.literal: They said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 它日識之，曰：「何故臥吹？」

translations.literal: Another day he recognized him and said: "Why do you play lying down?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day he recognized the man and asked, "Why are you playing lying down?"

sentences.zh: 笛工驚謝。

translations.literal: The flutist, startled, apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The flutist, startled, apologized.

sentences.zh: 又聞康昆侖奏琵琶，曰：「琵聲多，琶聲少，是未可彈五十四絲大弦也。」

translations.literal: Again he heard Kang Kunlun playing the pipa and said: "There is more pi-sound and less pa-sound — this will not do for the large strings of a fifty-four-string instrument."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Kang Kunlun play the pipa, he said, "There is more pi-sound than pa-sound. That will not do for the heavy strings of a fifty-four-string instrument."

sentences.zh: 樂家以自下逆鼓曰琵，自上順鼓曰琶云。

translations.literal: Musicians say that striking upward from below is called pi, and striking downward from above is called pa.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians explain that striking upward from below is called pi, and striking downward from above is called pa.

sentences.zh: 肅宗詔收群臣馬助戰，瑀與魏少遊等持不可。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong ordered the seizure of all ministers' horses to aid the war effort; Yu and Wei Shaoyou and others objected that this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong ordered the seizure of officials' horses for the war effort, Yu and Wei Shaoyou and others argued against it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，貶蓬州長史。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and demoted him to Chief Administrator of Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and demoted him to chief administrator of Peng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太子太師，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, with posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince and given the posthumous title Xuan, "Illustrious."

sentences.zh: 孫景儉。

translations.literal: His grandson Jing Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Jing Jian.

sentences.zh: 景儉字寬中。

translations.literal: Jing Jian, courtesy name Kuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Jian, courtesy name Kuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 及進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 強記多聞，善言古成敗王霸大略，高自負，於士大夫無所屈。

translations.literal: He had a strong memory and wide learning, was skilled at discussing the grand outlines of ancient success and failure, kingship and hegemony; he held himself very high and bowed to no scholar-official.
translations.idiomatic: He had a prodigious memory and wide learning, and loved to expound the grand patterns of ancient rise and fall, of kingship and hegemony. He thought highly of himself and deferred to no scholar-official.

sentences.zh: 王叔文等更譽之，以為管仲、諸葛亮比。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen and others praised him further, comparing him to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen and his circle praised him still more, comparing him to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 叔文敗，景儉以母喪得不坐。

translations.literal: When Shuwen was defeated, Jing Jian escaped punishment because he was in mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuwen fell, Jing Jian escaped punishment because he was in mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 韋夏卿守東都，辟幕府。

translations.literal: When Wei Xiaqing governed the Eastern Capital, he recruited Jing Jian to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Xiaqing governed the Eastern Capital, he brought Jing Jian onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 竇群任中丞，引為監察御史，群貶，景儉亦為江陵戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Dou Qun served as Censor-in-Chief, he brought him in as Investigating Censor; when Qun was demoted, Jing Jian became Clerk in the Household Section at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Qun became Censor-in-Chief, he made Jing Jian an investigating censor. After Qun was demoted, Jing Jian became a clerk in the household section at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 累擢忠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Governor of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to governor of Zhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元和末，入朝，不見用，復為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe era he entered court but was not employed, and again became Governor of Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuanhe era he came to court but found no favor, and was sent out again as governor of Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 素與元稹、李紳善。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Yuan Zhen and Li Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been close to Yuan Zhen and Li Shen.

sentences.zh: 二人方在翰林，言其才。

translations.literal: The two were then in the Hanlin Academy and spoke of his talent.
translations.idiomatic: The two were then in the Hanlin Academy and spoke up for his talent.

sentences.zh: 及延英奉辭，景儉自陳見抑遠，穆宗憐之，追詔為倉部員外郎，不遣。

translations.literal: When he took leave at Yanying Hall, Jing Jian stated that he had been suppressed and sent far away; Emperor Muzong pitied him and issued a recall appointing him Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau, but did not dispatch him.
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave at Yanying Hall, Jing Jian complained that he had been kept down and sent far away. Emperor Muzong took pity on him and issued a recall appointing him vice director in the Revenue Bureau—but never sent the order.

sentences.zh: 閱月，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After a month he was appointed Remonstrance and Review Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was appointed remonstrance and review grand master.

sentences.zh: 性矜誕，使酒縱氣，語侵宰相，蕭俯、段文昌訴於帝，貶建州刺史。

translations.literal: His nature was proud and unrestrained; when drunk he let loose his temper and his words insulted the chief ministers; Xiao Fu and Duan Wenchang complained to the Emperor, and he was demoted to Governor of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was proud and unrestrained by nature, and when drunk would speak with open contempt of the chief ministers. Xiao Fu and Duan Wenchang complained to the emperor, and he was demoted to governor of Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 稹得君，為之助，故還為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Zhen gained the emperor's favor, he helped him, and so he was restored as Remonstrance and Review Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zhen won the emperor's favor, he intervened on Jing Jian's behalf, and Jing Jian was restored as remonstrance and review grand master.

sentences.zh: 與馮宿、楊嗣復、溫造、李肇等集史官獨孤朗所，景儉醉，至中書，慢罵宰相王播、崔植、杜元穎，吏為遜言厚謝，乃去，坐貶漳州刺史，宿等皆逐矣。

translations.literal: With Feng Su, Yang Sifu, Wen Zao, Li Zhao, and others he gathered at the historian Du Gu Lang's house. Jing Jian, drunk, went to the Secretariat and insulted the chief ministers Wang Bo, Cui Zhi, and Du Yuanying. The clerks spoke deferentially and apologized profusely before he left. For this he was demoted to Governor of Zhang Prefecture, and Feng Su and the others were all expelled as well.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Feng Su, Yang Sifu, Wen Zao, Li Zhao, and others at the house of the historian Dugu Lang. Drunk, Jing Jian went to the Secretariat and reviled the chief ministers Wang Bo, Cui Zhi, and Du Yuanying. Only after the clerks spoke humbly and apologized at length did he leave. He was demoted to governor of Zhang Prefecture, and Feng Su and the others were driven out as well.

sentences.zh: 未及漳，稹輔政，改楚州刺史，議者謂景儉辱丞相，貶未至即遷，非是。

translations.literal: Before reaching Zhang Prefecture, Zhen came to power and changed his appointment to Governor of Chu Prefecture; critics said that since Jing Jian had insulted the chief minister, it was wrong to transfer him before the demotion had even taken effect.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Zhang Prefecture, Yuan Zhen came to power and changed the appointment to governor of Chu Prefecture. Critics said that since Jing Jian had insulted a chief minister, it was wrong to move him again before the demotion had even taken effect.

sentences.zh: 稹懼，改少府少監，悉還宿等。

translations.literal: Zhen feared the criticism and changed the appointment to Vice Director of the Palace Manufactories, and fully restored Feng Su and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the outcry, Yuan Zhen changed the appointment to vice director of the Palace Manufactories and fully restored Feng Su and the others.

sentences.zh: 景儉既湮厄不得志，卒。

translations.literal: Jing Jian, having been submerged in misfortune and unable to fulfill his ambitions, died.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Jian, submerged in misfortune and never able to fulfill his ambitions, died.

sentences.zh: 然其為人輕財，篤於義，既沒，士悵悼之。

translations.literal: Yet as a man he was generous with wealth and devoted to righteousness; after his death, scholars grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was generous with money and steadfast in friendship. When he died, men of learning mourned him.

sentences.zh: 惠莊太子捴，本名成義。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huizhuang Cou, original name Chengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huizhuang Cou had originally been named Chengyi.

sentences.zh: 初生，武后以母賤，欲不齒，以示浮屠萬回，回詭曰：「此西土樹神，宜兄弟。」

translations.literal: At birth, because Wu Hou considered his mother base-born and wished not to count him among her children, she showed him to the monk Wan Hui. Hui said deceitfully: "This is a tree deity of the Western Land — fit to be a brother."
translations.idiomatic: At his birth Empress Wu, deeming his mother too low in rank to count among her children, meant to disown him and showed him to the monk Wan Hui. Wan Hui said craftily, "This child is a tree deity of the Western Land—he is fit to be your brother."

sentences.zh: 後喜，乃畜之。

translations.literal: Afterwards she was pleased and raised him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was pleased and kept him.

sentences.zh: 垂拱三年，始王恒，與衛、趙二王同封。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chuigong he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Heng, together with the Princes of Wei and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chuigong he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Heng, together with the princes of Wei and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 俄改王衡陽。

translations.literal: Soon changed to Prince of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Prince of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，進王申，與岐、薛二王同封。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended, advanced to Prince of Shen, together with the Princes of Qi and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Cou was advanced to Prince of Shen, enfeoffed together with the princes of Qi and Xue.

sentences.zh: 累遷右衛、金吾二大將軍，實封至千戶。

translations.literal: Promoted in succession to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard and the Imperial Insignia Guard; actual fief reached a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to general-in-chief of the Right Guard and of the Imperial Insignia Guard, with an actual fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 進司徒，兼益州大都督，四為州刺史。

translations.literal: Advanced to Minister of Education, concurrently Grand Protector of Yizhou; served four times as prefectural governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to minister of education and concurrently made grand protector of Yizhou, and served four times as a prefectural governor.

sentences.zh: 開元八年，停刺史，復為司徒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan, when the governorships were discontinued, he again became Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan, when princes were no longer sent out as prefects, he again became minister of education.

sentences.zh: 薨，冊書贈太子及謚，陪葬橋陵。

translations.literal: He died; an edict conferred posthumous crown prince rank and title; buried alongside at Qiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, an edict conferred on him posthumous rank and title as crown prince, and he was buried beside Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 捴性寬裕，儀貌環重。

translations.literal: Cou's nature was magnanimous; his bearing was dignified and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Cou was magnanimous by nature, with a dignified and imposing bearing.

sentences.zh: 無嗣，詔以讓帝子珣嗣，為懷寧王，徙封同安。

translations.literal: Having no heirs, an edict appointed the Yielding Emperor's son Xun as successor, as Prince of Huaining, later transferred to Prince of Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heirs. An edict made the Yielding Emperor's son Xun his successor as Prince of Huaining, later transferred to Prince of Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，復以讓帝子璹嗣。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, again the Yielding Emperor's son Shu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era the Yielding Emperor's son Shu succeeded in his turn.

sentences.zh: 惠文太子範，始名隆範。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huiwen Fan, originally named Long Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huiwen Fan had originally been named Long Fan.

sentences.zh: 玄宗立，與薛王隆業避帝諱去二名。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended, he and Prince Xue Long Ye avoided the imperial taboo by dropping the second character of their names.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, he and Prince Xue Long Ye dropped the second character of their names to avoid the imperial taboo.

sentences.zh: 初王鄭，改封衛。

translations.literal: Initially Prince of Zheng, then changed to Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was first Prince of Zheng, then made Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 俄降封巴陵，進王岐，為太常卿、并州大都督、左羽林大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon demoted to Prince of Baling, then advanced to Prince of Qi; served as Minister of Rites, Grand Protector of Bingzhou, and General-in-Chief of the Left Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reduced to Prince of Baling, then advanced to Prince of Qi. He served as minister of rites, grand protector of Bingzhou, and general-in-chief of the Left Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 從玄宗誅太平公主，以功賜封，與薛王業並滿五千戶。

translations.literal: Following Xuanzong in executing Princess Taiping, rewarded with increased fief; together with Prince Xue Ye they each reached five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For following Xuanzong in the execution of Princess Taiping he was rewarded with increased fief; he and Prince Xue Ye each reached five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 歷為州刺史，遷太子太傅。

translations.literal: Served as prefectural governor in succession; transferred to Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as a prefectural governor and was then made grand mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 開元十四年薨，冊書贈太子及謚，陪葬橋陵。

translations.literal: Died in the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan; edict conferred posthumous crown prince rank and title; buried alongside at Qiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan. An edict conferred on him posthumous rank and title as crown prince, and he was buried beside Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 帝哭之慟，徹常膳至累旬，群臣勉請乃復。

translations.literal: The Emperor wept bitterly; regular meals were withdrawn for more than ten days until the ministers pressed him to resume.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept bitterly and refused his regular meals for more than ten days before the ministers pressed him to eat again.

sentences.zh: 範好學，工書，愛儒士，無貴賤為盡禮。

translations.literal: Fan loved learning, was skilled at calligraphy, cherished scholars; he showed full courtesy regardless of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fan loved learning, wrote well, and cherished scholars. He showed full courtesy to men of every rank.

sentences.zh: 與閻朝隱、劉廷琦、張諤、鄭繇等善，常飲酒賦詩相娛樂。

translations.literal: On good terms with Yan Chaoyin, Liu Tingqi, Zhang E, Zheng Yao, and others; they often drank wine and composed poetry for mutual enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Yan Chaoyin, Liu Tingqi, Zhang E, Zheng Yao, and others, and they often drank and wrote poetry together for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 又聚書畫，皆世所珍者。

translations.literal: He also collected books and paintings, all treasures of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He also collected books and paintings, all treasures of the age.

sentences.zh: 初，隋亡，禁內圖書湮放，唐興募訪，稍稍復出，藏秘府。

translations.literal: At first, when Sui fell, the palace library books were scattered and lost; when Tang rose, agents were sent to seek them, and gradually they reappeared and were stored in the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui fell, the palace library had been scattered and lost. After the Tang rose, the court sent out agents to seek the books, and little by little they reappeared and were stored in the secret archive.

sentences.zh: 長安初，張易之奏天下善工潢治，乃密使摹肖，殆不可辨，竊其真藏於家。

translations.literal: At the start of the Chang'an era, Zhang Yizhi petitioned that skilled craftsmen throughout the realm be summoned to mount and repair paintings. He secretly had copies made so faithful they could scarcely be told apart, and stole the originals to hide at home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chang'an era Zhang Yizhi petitioned to summon skilled craftsmen from across the realm to mount and repair paintings. Secretly he had copies made nearly indistinguishable from the originals and stole the true works for his own house.

sentences.zh: 既誅，悉為薛稷取去，稷又敗，範得之，後卒為火所焚。

translations.literal: After the Zhang brothers were executed, Xue Ji took them all; when Ji in turn fell, Fan obtained them, but in the end they were destroyed by fire.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhang brothers were executed, Xue Ji took them all. When Ji fell in his turn, Fan acquired the collection—but in the end it was destroyed by fire.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉裴虛己善讖緯，坐私與範遊，徙嶺南，廷琦貶雅州司戶，諤為山茌丞，然帝於範無少間也，謂左右曰：「兄弟情天至，於我豈有異哉！

translations.literal: The Empress's son-in-law Pei Xuji was versed in prophecy and apocrypha; for privately associating with Fan he was exiled to Lingnan, Liu Tingqi was demoted to registrar of Ya Prefecture, and Zhang E to magistrate of Shanzhi — yet the Emperor's regard for Fan did not diminish in the least, and he told those around him: "Brotherly feeling is heaven's own gift — how could mine be any different!
translations.idiomatic: The empress's son-in-law Pei Xuji was versed in prophecy and apocrypha. For privately associating with Fan he was exiled to Lingnan; Liu Tingqi was demoted to registrar of Ya Prefecture and Zhang E to magistrate of Shanzhi. Yet the emperor's affection for Fan did not waver in the least. He told those around him, "Brotherly feeling is heaven's own gift—how could mine be any different?

sentences.zh: 趨競者強相附，我終不以為纖介。」

translations.literal: Those who scramble for favor force themselves upon me, but I will never hold it against him for the slightest reason."
translations.idiomatic: Those who scramble for favor thrust themselves upon me, but I will never hold the least grudge against him for it."

sentences.zh: 時王毛仲等起賤微，暴貴，諸王見必加禮，獨範接之自如。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Maozhong and others rose from humble origins to sudden wealth; the princes all added ceremony when receiving them, but Fan alone treated them as naturally as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Maozhong and others had risen from humble origins to sudden wealth. The other princes always added ceremony when receiving them; Fan alone treated them as he always had.

sentences.zh: 子瑾嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 瑾落魄不飭名檢，沈酒色，歷太僕卿，封河東王，暴薨，贈太子少師。

translations.literal: Jin was unrestrained and careless of reputation, sunk in wine and women; he served as Grand Master of the Household for Horses, was enfeoffed as Prince of Hedong, and died suddenly; posthumously awarded Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was unrestrained and careless of reputation, sunk in wine and women. He served as grand master of the imperial stud and was enfeoffed as Prince of Hedong. He died suddenly and was posthumously made junior preceptor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，復以薛王子略陽公珍為嗣岐王。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, again Zhen, son of Prince Xue and Duke of Lueyang, succeeded as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era Prince Xue's son Zhen, Duke of Lueyang, again succeeded as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 珍儀觀豐偉，為宗正員外卿，與蔚州鎮將硃融善。

translations.literal: Zhen had a handsome and imposing presence; he served as vice director in the Court of the Imperial Clan and was on good terms with Zhu Rong, garrison commander of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was handsome and imposing. He served as vice director in the Court of the Imperial Clan and was close to Zhu Rong, garrison commander of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 融嘗言珍似上皇，因有陰謀，往語金吾將軍邢濟曰：「關外寇近，京師草草，奈何？」

translations.literal: Rong once said that Zhen resembled the Retired Emperor, and on that account formed a secret plot. He went to speak with Xing Ji, general of the Imperial Insignia Guard, saying: "The enemy beyond the passes is near, and the capital is in turmoil — what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Rong once said that Zhen resembled the Retired Emperor, and on that basis formed a secret plot. He went to the imperial insignia general Xing Ji and said, "The enemy beyond the passes is near and the capital is in turmoil. What is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「我金吾，天子押衙，以死生從，安自脫？」

translations.literal: Ji said: "I am of the Imperial Insignia Guard, the emperor's personal escort — I follow him in life and death. How could I save myself?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "I serve in the Imperial Insignia Guard, the emperor's personal escort. I follow him in life and death. How could I save myself?"

sentences.zh: 融曰：「見嗣岐王無慮矣。」

translations.literal: Rong said: "If you see the Heir Prince of Qi, you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "If you see the Heir Prince of Qi, you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 濟以聞，肅宗詔廢珍為庶人，賜死，融黨皆誅，擢濟為桂管防禦使。

translations.literal: Ji reported this. Emperor Suzong ordered Zhen reduced to commoner status and granted death; Rong's faction were all executed, and Ji was promoted to military commissioner of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji reported the matter. Emperor Suzong stripped Zhen of rank, made him a commoner, and ordered him to die. Rong's faction were all executed, and Ji was promoted to military commissioner of Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 惠宣太子業，始王趙，降封中山，授都水使者。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huixuan Ye, initially Prince of Zhao, reduced to Prince of Zhongshan, appointed Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huixuan Ye was first Prince of Zhao, then reduced to Prince of Zhongshan and appointed commissioner of waterways.

sentences.zh: 徙鼓城，兼陳州別駕，進王薛，為羽林大將軍、荊州大都督。

translations.literal: Transferred to Gucheng, concurrently Vice Prefect of Chen Prefecture; advanced to Prince of Xue; served as General-in-Chief of the Feathered Forest Guard and Grand Protector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gucheng and made concurrently vice prefect of Chen Prefecture, then advanced to Prince of Xue and appointed general-in-chief of the Feathered Forest Guard and grand protector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以好學授秘書監。

translations.literal: For his love of learning he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because he loved learning, he was appointed director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開元初，進太子少保，即拜太保，累歷州刺史。

translations.literal: At the start of Kaiyuan, advanced to Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince, then immediately appointed Grand Mentor; served as prefectural governor in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaiyuan era he was made junior mentor of the crown prince and then at once grand mentor, and served in succession as a prefectural governor.

sentences.zh: 初，母早終，從母賢妃鞠之。

translations.literal: At first his mother died early; his stepmother Consort Xian raised him.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had died early, and his stepmother Consort Xian raised him.

sentences.zh: 八年，迎賢妃外邸，事之甚謹。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he brought Consort Xian to an outer residence and served her with great reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he brought Consort Xian to an outer residence and served her with the utmost reverence.

sentences.zh: 其女弟淮陽、涼國二公主亦早卒，撫甥與己子均，帝益愛之。

translations.literal: His younger sisters, the Princesses of Huaiyang and Liang, also died early; he raised their sons as he did his own, and the Emperor loved him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sisters, the Princesses of Huaiyang and Liang, had also died early. He raised their sons exactly as he did his own, and the emperor loved him all the more.

sentences.zh: 嘗被疾，帝自祝禬。

translations.literal: Once when he fell ill, the Emperor himself prayed for his recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he fell ill, the emperor himself prayed for his recovery.

sentences.zh: 既愈，幸其第，置酒賦詩為初生歡。

translations.literal: When he recovered, the Emperor visited his residence, set out wine, and composed poetry in celebration of his return to health.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered, the emperor visited his residence, set out wine, and composed poetry to celebrate his return to health.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗不豫，業妃弟內直郎韋賓與殿中監皇甫恂妄言休咎事，賓坐死，恂貶錦州刺史。

translations.literal: Once when the Emperor was unwell, Ye's wife's younger brother, Inner Attendant Wei Bin, and the Palace Director Huangfu Xun spoke recklessly of fortune and misfortune; Bin was executed for the offense, and Xun was demoted to governor of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor was unwell, Ye's wife's younger brother, inner attendant Wei Bin, and the palace director Huangfu Xun spoke recklessly of fortune and misfortune. Bin was executed, and Xun was demoted to governor of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 妃恐，降服待罪，業亦不敢入謁，帝聞，遽召之，業伏殿下請罪，帝趨就執其手曰：「吾所猜於兄弟者，天地共咎之！」

translations.literal: The princess feared punishment, wore mourning garb and awaited judgment; Ye also dared not enter to pay court. When the Emperor heard of it, he summoned them at once. Ye prostrated himself below the hall steps to beg forgiveness; the Emperor hastened down and took his hand, saying: "Any suspicion I harbor against my brothers — let heaven and earth together condemn it!"
translations.idiomatic: The princess, afraid, wore mourning garb and awaited punishment; Ye too dared not come to court. When the emperor heard of it he summoned them at once. Ye prostrated himself below the hall steps to beg forgiveness. The emperor hurried down and took his hand, saying, "Any suspicion I harbor against my brothers, let heaven and earth together condemn!"

sentences.zh: 遂復燕歡，仍諭妃復位。

translations.literal: Thereupon they resumed their feast, and the Emperor also ordered the princess to resume her rank.
translations.idiomatic: They resumed their feast, and the emperor also ordered the princess to resume her rank.

sentences.zh: 俄進司徒。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was advanced to minister of education.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，業有疾，帝憂之，一昔容發為變，因假寢，夢獲方，寤而業少閑，邠王守禮等請以事付史官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Ye fell ill; the Emperor worried over him, and in a single night his countenance and hair changed. While napping he dreamed of obtaining a prescription; when he awoke Ye had slightly improved. Prince of Bin Shouli and others asked that the matter be committed to the historians.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Ye fell ill. The emperor worried so deeply that in a single night his face and hair seemed to age. He napped and dreamed of obtaining a prescription; when he awoke Ye had slightly improved. Prince of Bin Shouli and others asked that the affair be recorded by the historians.

sentences.zh: 及薨，帝悲不能食，冊書加贈及謚，陪葬橋陵。

translations.literal: When Ye died, the Emperor grieved until he could not eat; an edict added posthumous honors and title; buried alongside at Qiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye died, the emperor grieved until he could not eat. An edict added posthumous honors and title, and Ye was buried beside Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 十一子，其聞者瑗、瑒、琄。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons; those of note were Yuan, Yang, and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons; those worth recording were Yuan, Yang, and Xuan.

sentences.zh: 帝後追思業，引見瑗等，傷之，乃下詔共賜實封千戶。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor recalled Ye with longing, summoned Yuan and the others to audience, was grieved, and issued an edict jointly granting them a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Emperor, remembering Ye with longing, summoned Yuan and the others, was deeply moved, and issued an edict jointly granting them a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 瑗為樂安王。

translations.literal: Yuan was Prince of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was made Prince of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 瑒滎陽王、宗正卿。

translations.literal: Yang was Prince of Xingyang and Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was Prince of Xingyang and Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 琄為嗣薛王，歷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Xuan was successor Prince of Xue and served as Minister of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was successor Prince of Xue and served as Minister of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，琄舅韋堅為李林甫所構，坐貶夷陵別駕，徙置夜郎、南浦。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, Xuan's uncle Wei Jian was framed by Li Linfu, demoted to Vice Prefect of Yiling, and transferred to Yelang and Nanpu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, Xuan's uncle Wei Jian was framed by Li Linfu, demoted to Vice Prefect of Yiling, and transferred to Yelang and Nanpu.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山亂，乃還京師。

translations.literal: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, he then returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 曾孫知柔，嗣王，再為宗正卿。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Zhirou succeeded to the princedom and twice served as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Zhirou succeeded to the princedom and twice served as Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢京兆尹。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to Governor of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was promoted to Governor of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 始，鄭、白渠梗壅，民不得歲。

translations.literal: At first the Zheng and Bai canals were blocked and silted; the people could not harvest.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Zheng and Bai canals were blocked and silted, and the people could not bring in their harvests.

sentences.zh: 知柔調三輔，治復舊道，灌浸如約，遂無旱虞，民詣闕請立石紀功，知柔固讓得止。

translations.literal: Zhirou regulated the three metropolitan districts, restored the old channels, and irrigation followed the agreements; thereafter there was no fear of drought; the people went to court requesting a stone monument to record the achievement, but Zhirou firmly declined and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou regulated the three metropolitan districts, restored the old channels, and irrigation met its quotas; thereafter drought ceased to be a threat. The people petitioned at court for a stone monument to record his achievement, but Zhirou firmly declined and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 加累檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively made Acting Grand Preceptor and Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was cumulatively appointed Acting Grand Preceptor and Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 又詔營緝太廟，判度支，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to repair the Grand Ancestral Temple, to oversee the Department of Revenue, and to serve as Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to repair the Grand Ancestral Temple, to oversee the Department of Revenue, and to serve as Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport in all circuits.

sentences.zh: 昭宗出莎城，獨知柔從，乘輿器用庖頓皆主之，大細畢給。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong left Shacheng, only Zhirou followed; he was in charge of the imperial carriage, utensils, and kitchen supplies, and great and small were all provided.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong fled Shacheng, only Zhirou accompanied him; he oversaw the imperial carriage, utensils, and provisions, and everything great and small was supplied.

sentences.zh: 性儉約，雖位通顯，無居第。

translations.literal: By nature frugal and abstemious, though his rank was eminent, he had no residence of his own.
translations.idiomatic: By nature frugal and abstemious, though his rank was eminent, he owned no house of his own.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出拜清海軍節度使，在鎮廉潔，貢獻時入，進檢校太傅，兼侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as Military Commissioner of Qinghai Army; in his command he was honest and clean, tribute was regularly sent in, and he was advanced to Acting Grand Tutor and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted as Military Commissioner of the Qinghai Army; in his command he was honest and incorrupt, tribute arrived on schedule, and he was advanced to Acting Grand Tutor and concurrently Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 仕凡四紀，常為宗室冠。

translations.literal: In office for four reign-periods in all, he was constantly foremost among the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: He served through four reign-periods in all and was constantly foremost among the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮。

translations.literal: He died in his command.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his command.

sentences.zh: 隋王隆悌，始封汝南王。

translations.literal: Prince Sui Longti was first enfeoffed Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sui Longti was first enfeoffed as Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 早薨，睿宗追王，贈荊州大都督，爵不傳。

translations.literal: He died young; Ruizong posthumously enfeoffed him as prince and granted the posthumous title Grand Military Commissioner of Jing Prefecture; the title was not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He died young; Ruizong posthumously enfeoffed him as prince and granted the posthumous title Grand Military Commissioner of Jing Prefecture; the title was not transmitted.

sentences.zh: 【贊】贊曰：中宗失道，身為母所廢，妻所弒，而四子皆不得其死，嗣亦不傳，殆天穢其德而絕之，何耶？

translations.literal: [Eulogy] The eulogy says: Zhongzong lost the Way; his person was deposed by his mother and murdered by his wife; his four sons all failed to die natural deaths, and the succession too was not transmitted—perhaps Heaven reviled his virtue and cut him off; why?
translations.idiomatic: [Eulogy] The eulogy says: Zhongzong lost the Way; he was deposed by his mother and murdered by his wife; all four of his sons met unnatural deaths, and the succession too was cut off—perhaps Heaven reviled his virtue and ended his line. Why else?

sentences.zh: 彼固自絕於天云爾。

translations.literal: They had indeed cut themselves off from Heaven—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: They had cut themselves off from Heaven—that is all.

sentences.zh: 睿宗有聖子，一受命，一追帝，三贈太子，天與之報，福流無窮，盛歟！

translations.literal: Ruizong had sage sons: one received the Mandate, one was posthumously made emperor, three were posthumously made crown princes—Heaven's reward to him; blessings flowed without end—how splendid!
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong had sage sons: one received the Mandate, one was posthumously made emperor, three were posthumously made crown princes—Heaven's reward to him; blessings flowed without end—how splendid!
